commonErrors.error: Defender blocks every option
commonErrors.correction: Reduce defender speed or increase target spacing.

progressions: Reduce the distance between defender and kicker.
Require the non-preferred foot for one side.
Add a time limit for disposal.
regressions: Tell the defender which option to block.
Allow the kicker to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Avoid forcing the football into pressure.
matchApplication: Ball carriers regularly need to choose between several targets while opponents block or close passing lanes. This drill applies to: Defensive exits. Forward entries. Midfield possession. Switching play. Kicking from congestion.

title: Smother Pressure Kick
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and avoid a potential smother before executing a kick. Players learn to alter the kicking angle, delay briefly or move laterally to create a safe disposal lane.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one attacker’s cone and one defender’s cone approximately six to eight metres apart.
• Place two kicking gates, one left and one right of the defender.
• Position a receiver 20–25 metres beyond each gate.
• The attacker begins with the football.
• The defender begins facing the attacker.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. On the coach’s signal, the attacker moves forward.
2. The defender closes and raises the hands to threaten a smother.
3. The attacker reads the defender’s movement.
4. The attacker creates a safe kicking lane by:
5. Moving slightly left or right.
6. Taking an extra step.
7. Delaying until the defender loses balance.
8. The attacker kicks through one of the two gates to a receiver.
9. The defender attempts a controlled smother without contacting the kicking leg.
10. Players rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Recognise the smothering line.
Avoid kicking directly through raised hands.
Use small lateral movements.
Keep the football secure.
Prepare early.
Remain balanced.
Complete the kick only when the lane is clear.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players expose the kicking leg.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks directly into raised hands
commonErrors.correction: Move off the defender’s line before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Attacker panics and throws the ball onto the boot
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a controlled ball drop.

commonErrors.error: Player makes an excessively wide evasion
commonErrors.correction: Use a small movement to preserve balance.

commonErrors.error: Defender dives dangerously at the kicking leg
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce controlled smother technique and safe spacing.

commonErrors.error: Attacker holds the football too long
commonErrors.correction: Prepare early and use the first safe lane.

progressions: Allow the defender to recover after the first evasion.
regressions: Tell the attacker which side to use.
Have the defender hold a hit shield rather than attempt a smother.
matchApplication: Smother pressure commonly occurs when players: Exit congestion. Kick from stoppages. Deliver inside 50. Receive near an opponent. Attempt defensive clearances.

title: Time-Limited Kick
objective: Develop the ability to scan, select a target and execute an accurate kick within a limited period. Players learn to prepare before possession and avoid wasting time once the football is secured.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one central receiving cone.
• Position three targets approximately 20 metres away at different angles.
• A feeder stands 10–15 metres from the central receiver.
• Players form lines at the feeder, receiver and target positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The receiver scans the target positions.
2. The feeder passes the football to the receiver.
3. As the football arrives, the coach begins a countdown.
4. The receiver must select and kick to a target within the allowed time.
5. Recommended time limits:
6. Under 12: Four seconds.
7. Under 14: Three seconds.
8. Under 16 and above: Two to three seconds.
9. The selected target marks or gathers the football.
10. Players rotate positions.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before receiving.
Know the available targets.
Prepare the football immediately.
Take only the steps required.
Remain calm under the countdown.
Select a simple option.
Maintain technical quality.

commonErrors.error: Player waits until possession to scan
commonErrors.correction: Identify targets before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: Kicker rushes the ball drop
commonErrors.correction: Keep the technique controlled despite the countdown.

commonErrors.error: Player searches for the perfect option
commonErrors.correction: Use the first safe and effective target.

commonErrors.error: Too many steps are taken
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the football immediately after possession.

commonErrors.error: Time limit causes repeated failure
commonErrors.correction: Add one second until players regain confidence.

progressions: Remove one option on the coach’s call.
Require the non-preferred foot for selected targets.
Begin with a ground ball gather.
regressions: Allow the receiver to begin with the football.
matchApplication: Players often have limited time after: Taking possession in traffic. Receiving at half-back. Winning a clearance. Marking and playing on. Collecting a loose football.

title: Kick Under Side Pressure
objective: Develop the ability to execute an effective kick while pressure arrives from the side. Players learn to protect the football, maintain their line and avoid being pushed across the intended target.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple lanes
setup:
• Create a straight running lane.
• Place:
• An attacker’s starting cone.
• A defender’s starting cone three metres to the attacker’s left or right.
• A kicking line 10–12 metres ahead.
• A receiving target 20–30 metres beyond the kicking line.
• The attacker begins with the football.
• The defender begins slightly behind and to the side.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. On the coach’s signal, both players begin.
2. The attacker runs towards the kicking line.
3. The defender applies controlled side pressure using body positioning or a hit shield.
4. The attacker protects the football and maintains forward movement.
5. The attacker prepares and kicks to the target.
6. The defender avoids contacting the kicking leg.
7. Players rotate roles.
8. Repeat with pressure arriving from both sides.
9. The contact level must remain appropriate to the group.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Keep the football on the side away from pressure.
Maintain a strong running line.
Use the body to protect possession.
Avoid leaning excessively into the defender.
Regain balance before the final step.
Align the kick with the target.
Continue moving after disposal.

commonErrors.error: Football is carried on the pressure side
commonErrors.correction: Move the football to the protected side of the body.

commonErrors.error: Attacker drifts away from the target
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a stronger forward line.

commonErrors.error: Player leans heavily into the defender
commonErrors.correction: Keep the feet active and remain upright enough to kick.

commonErrors.error: Kick travels across the body
commonErrors.correction: Regain alignment before the final step.

commonErrors.error: Defender contacts the kicking leg
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce controlled pressure and safe positioning.

regressions: Replace the defender with a hit shield held by a coach.
Allow the attacker to stop before kicking.
successIndicators: Perform effectively from both pressure sides.
matchApplication: Lateral pressure occurs when players: Run along the boundary. Exit congestion. Receive an overlap handball. Break from a tackle. Carry the football through traffic.

title: One-Step Kick
objective: Develop the ability to execute an accurate drop punt using only one controlled step. Players learn to prepare the football early and use a compact kicking action when time and space are limited.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 8–20
Maximum: Unlimited, working in pairs
setup:
• Players work in pairs facing each other.
• Recommended distances:
• Under 12–14: 10–12 metres.
• Under 16 and above: 12–18 metres.
• Place one kicking cone in front of each player.
• The football begins with one player.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A receives or begins with the football.
2. Player A prepares the ball immediately.
3. Player A takes one controlled step.
4. Player A executes a drop punt to Player B.
5. Player B marks or gathers the football.
6. Player B repeats the same one-step kick.
7. Continue for the allocated time.
8. Alternate preferred and non-preferred feet where appropriate.
9. Players must not add extra approach steps.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Prepare the football before stepping.
Keep the step short and balanced.
Maintain the head over the ball.
Use a compact but complete leg swing.
Guide the football directly onto the boot.
Finish towards the target.
Prioritise clean contact over power.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the kick becomes short and stabbing.

commonErrors.error: Player takes several steps
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the football earlier and use one controlled step.

commonErrors.error: Final step is too long
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the step to remain balanced.

commonErrors.error: Kick becomes a stabbing motion
commonErrors.correction: Complete the leg swing through the football.

commonErrors.error: Player leans backwards
commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest over the ball.

commonErrors.error: Accuracy falls at longer distances
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the distance and rebuild clean technique.

regressions: Rehearse the preparation and step without kicking.
matchApplication: One-step kicks are required when players have limited space after: A ground-ball gather. A handball receive. A stoppage release. A mark close to pressure. Turning away from an opponent.

title: Boundary-Line Kick
primarySkill: Kicking from a Restricted Boundary Position
objective: Develop the ability to kick effectively when the boundary line limits the player’s available movement and passing angle. Players learn to protect the football, open the body and select a safe target without stepping out of bounds.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Use a painted boundary line or create one with cones.
• Place the kicker approximately one metre inside the boundary.
• Position three receiving targets:
• One short and inside.
• One longer along the boundary.
• One central target at a wider angle.
• A feeder stands behind or inside the kicker.
• Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder passes the football to the kicker near the boundary.
2. The kicker scans the available targets.
3. The coach may nominate one target as unavailable.
4. The kicker adjusts body position without crossing the boundary.
5. The kicker selects and delivers to the best available target.
6. The receiver marks or gathers the football.
7. Players rotate positions.
8. Repeat from both sides of the ground.
9. Players should practise kicking from both left and right boundaries.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Know where the boundary is.
Keep the football protected on the inside.
Open the hips towards the selected target.
Avoid drifting out of bounds.
Use the safest available option.
Maintain balance in restricted space.
Use an appropriate kick for the angle.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players repeatedly choose the same option.

commonErrors.error: Player steps out of bounds
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the movement and stay aware of the line.

commonErrors.error: Kicker closes the body towards the boundary
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the inside target.

commonErrors.error: Player forces a kick down the line
commonErrors.correction: Scan for safer central or short options.

commonErrors.error: Ball is exposed towards pressure
commonErrors.correction: Keep it on the protected inside side.

commonErrors.error: Kicker loses balance in restricted space
commonErrors.correction: Reduce foot movement and set the base before kicking.

progressions: Reduce available space near the boundary.
Add a kick around the mark.
regressions: Tell the player which option to use.
Allow the player to begin stationary with the football.
successIndicators: Deliver accurate kicks from both boundaries.
matchApplication: Boundary-line kicking occurs during: General play. Marks near the line. Defensive exits. Wing possession. Forward-pocket entries. Kicks after boundary-side ground balls.

title: Quick Release Kick
objective: Develop the ability to receive possession and execute an accurate kick with minimal delay. Players learn to scan before receiving, prepare the football immediately and complete the disposal before nearby pressure can arrive.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three positions:
• Feeder.
• Central receiver.
• Two final targets.
• Place the feeder approximately 10–15 metres from the central receiver.
• Place the final targets approximately 15–25 metres beyond the receiver, one to the left and one to the right.
• Players form lines at each position.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The receiver scans both final targets.
2. The feeder passes the football to the receiver.
3. As the football travels, the coach calls either “left” or “right.”
4. The receiver secures possession.
5. The receiver prepares the football immediately.
6. The receiver takes no more than one or two steps.
7. The receiver kicks to the nominated target.
8. Players rotate through each position.
9. Continue for the allocated time.
10. The coach may progressively delay the directional call to increase difficulty.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan both targets before receiving.
Present the hands early.
Secure the football cleanly.
Move it immediately into kicking position.
Keep the preparation compact.
Use one balanced step where possible.
Maintain accuracy despite the reduced time.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players rush the ball drop.
Whether the time pressure is appropriate.

commonErrors.error: Player waits until receiving before scanning
commonErrors.correction: Identify both targets before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: Receiver takes too many steps
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the football immediately and use a compact approach.

commonErrors.error: Ball drop becomes rushed
commonErrors.correction: Keep the hands controlled and guide the football onto the boot.

commonErrors.error: Player guesses the target before the call
commonErrors.correction: Remain balanced and react to the coach’s direction.

commonErrors.error: Accuracy decreases significantly
commonErrors.correction: Slow the drill and rebuild clean execution.

progressions: Require non-preferred foot use for one side.
Begin with a ground ball or handball receive.
regressions: Call the target before the feed.
Allow the receiver to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Deliver accurate kicks to both sides.
matchApplication: Quick release kicks are required when players receive near pressure during: Stoppage exits. Forward-half turnovers. Defensive rebounds. Handball chains. Short marks followed by immediate play-on.
relatedDrills: KK-037 – Mark, Play On and Kick

title: Kick Around the Mark
primarySkill: Kicking Around a Player on the Mark
objective: Develop the ability to create a clear kicking lane around a player standing the mark. Players learn to move laterally with control, maintain balance and deliver accurately without drifting excessively or crossing the mark.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
equipment: Bibs for players on the mark.
setup:
• Place one kicking cone and one mark cone approximately five metres apart.
• Position two receiving targets 20–30 metres away:
• One to the left.
• One to the right.
• A player stands on the mark cone.
• The kicker begins behind the kicking cone with the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker scans both target options.
2. The player on the mark holds position with arms raised.
3. The kicker moves laterally to either side.
4. The kicker creates a clear lane around the mark.
5. The kicker balances and delivers to the selected target.
6. The receiver marks or gathers the football.
7. Players rotate through kicker, mark and receiver roles.
8. Continue from both sides.
9. The player on the mark may initially remain stationary before introducing controlled lateral movement.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before moving.
Use controlled lateral steps.
Keep the football secure.
Create only the space required.
Align the hips and shoulders with the target.
Avoid leaning backwards while moving sideways.
Complete the kick before the mark closes the angle.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player on the mark remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: Kicker moves too far sideways
commonErrors.correction: Create only enough angle to clear the mark.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks while still drifting
commonErrors.correction: Balance and square the body before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Kicker watches only the mark
commonErrors.correction: Scan the targets before beginning the movement.

commonErrors.error: Football is exposed near the mark
commonErrors.correction: Keep it protected until the kicking action begins.

commonErrors.error: Player on the mark moves illegally or dangerously
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce passive, controlled pressure.

progressions: Allow the player on the mark to move laterally.
Reduce the distance between kicker and mark.
Require the non-preferred foot on one side.
Add a second defender closing from behind.
regressions: Use a stationary pole instead of a player.
Increase the starting distance from the mark.
Tell the kicker which side to use.
Allow the kicker to stop completely before kicking.
successIndicators: Deliver accurate kicks to both sides.
matchApplication: Players regularly need to kick around the mark after: Taking a mark. Receiving a free kick. Playing near the boundary. Switching direction. Attempting a short-angle pass.
relatedDrills: KK-037 – Mark, Play On and Kick

title: Mark, Play On and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to mark the football, recognise available space and play on quickly before executing an accurate kick. Players learn to prepare the next action before the mark is completed.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three positions:
• Feeder.
• Marking player.
• Final target.
• Place the feeder and marking player approximately 15 metres apart.
• Place two play-on gates, one left and one right of the marking player.
• Place the final target 20–30 metres beyond the gates.
• Players form lines at all three positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The marking player scans both play-on gates.
2. The feeder kicks to the marking player.
3. The player marks the football.
4. The coach calls “left” or “right.”
5. The player plays on through the nominated gate.
6. The player accelerates for several steps.
7. The player kicks to the final target.
8. Players rotate through each position.
9. Continue for the allocated time.
10. The directional call may be made before or immediately after the mark depending on the group’s ability.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before marking.
Mark the football cleanly.
Land balanced.
Turn quickly towards the selected gate.
Accelerate into space.
Prepare the football early.
Maintain accuracy while playing on.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players drift outside the gate.

commonErrors.error: Player marks flat-footed
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the feet and land ready to move.

commonErrors.error: Player turns before securing the mark
commonErrors.correction: Complete the mark before playing on.

commonErrors.error: Play-on movement is slow
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately through the gate.

commonErrors.error: Football is prepared too late
commonErrors.correction: Move it into kicking position during the first steps.

commonErrors.error: Player rushes the final kick
commonErrors.correction: Control the last steps before disposal.

progressions: Add a player on the mark.
Require non-preferred foot use on one side.
Allow the player to choose whether to play on.
regressions: Call the direction before the kick arrives.
Allow the player to walk through the pattern.
Begin with a handball feed instead of a kick.
successIndicators: Complete the sequence without unnecessary delay.
matchApplication: Mark-and-play-on situations occur when players: Take an uncontested mark. Recognise open space. Move the ball quickly through defence. Attack through the corridor. Create a fast forward entry.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick

title: Side-Step from the Mark
objective: Develop the ability to use a controlled side-step to move around a player on the mark before executing an accurate kick. Players learn to shift the defender, protect the football and regain alignment quickly.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
equipment: Bibs for players on the mark.
setup:
• Place one kicker behind a mark cone.
• Position a player on the mark approximately five metres away.
• Place two receiving targets 20–25 metres beyond the mark, one left and one right.
• The kicker begins with the football.
• Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker approaches the mark under control.
2. The kicker uses a small side-step or body feint.
3. The player on the mark reacts but does not tackle.
4. The kicker moves into the created lane.
5. The kicker regains balance.
6. The kicker delivers to one of the two targets.
7. Players rotate positions.
8. Practise side-stepping in both directions.
9. The kicker should avoid running too close to the mark.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Approach with balanced speed.
Keep the football secure.
Use the hips, shoulders and eyes to sell the feint.
Take a decisive step into the new lane.
Avoid excessive sideways movement.
Square the body before kicking.
Maintain a compact ball drop.

commonErrors.error: Side-step is too wide
commonErrors.correction: Use one decisive movement into the new lane.

commonErrors.error: Player loses control of the football
commonErrors.correction: Keep it secure with two hands during the evasion.

commonErrors.error: Kicker disposes while moving sideways
commonErrors.correction: Regain alignment before the final step.

commonErrors.error: Feint does not move the defender
commonErrors.correction: Use the eyes, shoulders and hips to sell the first direction.

commonErrors.error: Player approaches too close to the mark
commonErrors.correction: Begin the evasive movement earlier.

progressions: Allow the mark to apply controlled contact.
regressions: Replace the player with a pole.
Tell the kicker which direction to step.
Allow the player to stop before kicking.
successIndicators: Move the mark with the feint.
Perform the movement in both directions.
matchApplication: Side-stepping the mark can create: A clearer kicking lane. A better angle inside 50. Space to use the non-preferred side. A corridor option. Time to avoid a smother.
relatedDrills: KK-037 – Mark, Play On and Kick
KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick

title: Short Mark and Switch Kick
objective: Develop the ability to mark the football, scan across the ground and switch play to a target positioned away from the original direction of the pass.
players:
Minimum: 7
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three positions in an angled pattern:
• Feeder.
• Central marking player.
• Switch target positioned 20–30 metres to the opposite side.
• Place an optional second target directly ahead to create a visual alternative.
• Players form lines at each position.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The central player scans towards the switch target.
2. The feeder kicks to the central player.
3. The central player marks the football.
4. The player turns away from the direction of the original pass.
5. The player balances and kicks to the switch target.
6. The switch target marks the football.
7. Players rotate through all positions.
8. Reverse the direction after several minutes.
9. The coach may occasionally call for the direct target to keep players scanning both options.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before the mark.
Mark with the body prepared to turn.
Secure the football before changing direction.
Use short turning steps.
Open the hips towards the switch target.
Balance before disposal.
Kick to the target’s advantage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players automatically kick straight ahead.

commonErrors.error: Player does not scan before marking
commonErrors.correction: Check the switch target while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Receiver turns before securing possession
commonErrors.correction: Complete the mark first.

commonErrors.error: Body remains closed to the switch
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips and shoulders before kicking.

commonErrors.error: Switch kick travels behind the target
commonErrors.correction: Kick to the receiver’s advantage.

commonErrors.error: Player takes too long to move the football
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the turn before possession.

progressions: Add a player on the mark.
Allow the player to choose between direct and switch options.
regressions: Tell the player the switch direction.
Allow the player to stop after turning.
successIndicators: Move the football without unnecessary delay.
matchApplication: Switching play is used to: Move away from defensive pressure. Access the open side. Change the angle of attack. Exit defence. Create uncontested possession.
relatedDrills: KK-037 – Mark, Play On and Kick
KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Fake and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to use the eyes, shoulders and body position to move a defender before delivering the football to another target. Players learn to disguise their intended option without compromising kicking technique.
players:
Minimum: 8
Ideal: 12–20
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one central kicker with two receiving targets approximately 20–25 metres away, one left and one right.
• Position one passive defender five to eight metres in front of the kicker.
• A feeder stands behind the kicker with the football.
• Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder passes to the kicker.
2. The kicker scans both targets.
3. The kicker uses the eyes, shoulders or a short body movement to suggest one option.
4. The defender reacts towards the fake.
5. The kicker resets the body.
6. The kicker delivers to the opposite target.
7. Players rotate through each role.
8. Vary the direction of the fake.
9. The fake should be controlled and believable.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan both targets before the fake.
Use the eyes and shoulders to sell the first option.
Keep the football secure.
Avoid overcommitting the body.
Regain balance quickly.
Align with the real target.
Complete the kick with normal technique.

commonErrors.error: Fake is too small to move the defender
commonErrors.correction: Use clearer eyes and shoulder movement.

commonErrors.error: Player overcommits and loses balance
commonErrors.correction: Keep the feet controlled and the body centred.

commonErrors.error: Football is moved loosely during the fake
commonErrors.correction: Hold it securely until the real kicking action begins.

commonErrors.error: Defender does not react
commonErrors.correction: Improve the timing and realism of the first option.

commonErrors.error: Real kick becomes rushed
commonErrors.correction: Reset the body before disposal.

progressions: Allow the defender to choose whether to react.
regressions: Use a coach as the defender.
Allow the kicker to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Move the defender with the fake.
matchApplication: Fakes are used to: Move a player on the mark. Open a corridor kick. Create a switch option. Avoid a smother. Disguise a forward entry. Create time in congestion.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick
KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Switch Kick to Moving Target
primarySkill: Switching Play to a Moving Receiver
objective: Develop the ability to recognise a switch opportunity and deliver accurately to a teammate moving into open space on the opposite side of the ground. Players learn to scan early, open the body and weight the kick so the receiver can maintain momentum.
players:
Minimum: 7
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize: Medium to Large Area Approximately 45 m × 35 m
setup:
• Create three main positions:
• Initial feeder.
• Central receiver.
• Switch receiver.
• Place the feeder and central receiver approximately 15 metres apart.
• Position the switch receiver’s starting cone 20–30 metres away on the opposite side and slightly forward of the central player.
• Place a target cone another five to ten metres ahead of the switch receiver’s starting position.
• Players form lines at each position.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The central player scans towards the switch side.
2. The feeder kicks to the central player.
3. As the football travels, the switch receiver begins moving towards the target cone.
4. The central player marks the football.
5. The central player opens the body towards the switch.
6. The central player delivers the football into the receiver’s running path.
7. The switch receiver marks while continuing forward.
8. Players rotate through all positions.
9. Reverse the switching direction after several minutes.
10. The receiver should not stop and wait underneath the football.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the switch side before receiving.
Mark with the body ready to open.
Turn using short, balanced steps.
Identify the receiver’s speed and direction.
Kick to where the receiver is going.
Use appropriate height and weight.
Avoid floating the football unnecessarily.

commonErrors.error: Central player does not scan before receiving
commonErrors.correction: Check the switch side while the first kick is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Receiver begins the run too early
commonErrors.correction: Delay until the ball is moving towards the central player.

commonErrors.error: Switch kick travels behind the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Aim further into the running path.

commonErrors.error: Kick hangs in the air
commonErrors.correction: Use a flatter trajectory where appropriate.

commonErrors.error: Central player takes too long to turn
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the body before completing the mark.

progressions: Add a player on the mark.
Allow the receiver to choose between two running lanes.
Require non-preferred foot use in one direction.
regressions: Tell the receiver when and where to move.
Allow the central player additional preparation time.
successIndicators: Allow the receiver to maintain momentum.
matchApplication: This drill develops switching play during: Defensive exits. Half-back ball movement. Wing transitions. Changes of attacking angle. Movement away from a congested side.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick

title: Long Switch Kick
objective: Develop the ability to execute a longer switch kick across the ground while maintaining accuracy and appropriate trajectory. Players learn to generate distance through controlled technique rather than sacrificing balance.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one kicking position near one side of the ground.
• Create a large receiving target zone 35–50 metres away on the opposite side.
• Place a receiver inside the target zone.
• A feeder stands approximately 10 metres from the kicker.
• Players form lines at feeder, kicker and receiver positions.
• Adjust distance according to age and kicking capability.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker scans the target zone.
2. The feeder passes to the kicker.
3. The kicker marks or gathers the football.
4. The kicker turns towards the opposite side.
5. The kicker uses a controlled approach.
6. The kicker delivers a long kick into the target zone.
7. The receiver marks or gathers.
8. Players rotate positions.
9. Practise switching in both directions.
10. Players score one point when the kick lands inside the target zone and two points when the receiver marks it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Align the entire body with the target.
Use a smooth approach.
Maintain a controlled ball drop.
Generate power through leg speed and follow-through.
Avoid leaning backwards.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Use enough height to clear pressure without allowing excessive hang time.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Difference between preferred and non-preferred directions.

commonErrors.error: Player leans backwards for distance
commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest over the football and drive through the kick.

commonErrors.error: Kick has excessive height and little distance
commonErrors.correction: Improve contact and increase leg speed.

commonErrors.error: Ball drifts across the ground
commonErrors.correction: Align the hips and shoulders before the approach.

commonErrors.error: Player overkicks and loses accuracy
commonErrors.correction: Reduce effort slightly and restore clean technique.

commonErrors.error: Receiver waits at the back of the zone
commonErrors.correction: Position to move towards the football.

progressions: Add a player on the mark.
regressions: Allow the kicker to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Land kicks inside the target zone.
Give the receiver a realistic marking opportunity.
matchApplication: Long switch kicks are used to: Move the football away from defensive congestion. Access the open side. Change the angle of attack. Exit defensive 50. Transfer play across half-back.
relatedDrills: KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Defensive Exit Switch
objective: Develop the ability to switch the football from a defensive position when the direct side is congested. Players learn to recognise pressure, use a safe release option and move the football towards the open side.
setup:
• Create four positions:
• Defensive ball carrier near one boundary.
• Short central release target.
• Opposite-side switch target.
• Final outlet target further up the ground.
• Place one passive defender near the direct-side option to represent congestion.
• Players form lines at each attacking position.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The defensive ball carrier begins with the football.
2. The defender positions to discourage the direct kick.
3. The ball carrier scans the central and opposite-side options.
4. The ball carrier kicks to the short central release target.
5. The central player marks and immediately opens towards the opposite side.
6. The central player kicks to the switch target.
7. The switch target marks and delivers to the final outlet.
8. Players follow their disposals and rotate.
9. Repeat from the opposite boundary.
10. The drill should move the football away from pressure rather than through it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Recognise when the direct side is blocked.
Use the safe release player.
Scan before receiving.
Position the body to continue the switch.
Maintain width.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Move immediately after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Initial decision by the defensive player.
Whether players force the direct option.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier forces the kick down the congested side
commonErrors.correction: Use the central release and switch away from pressure.

commonErrors.error: Central player receives with a closed body
commonErrors.correction: Position side-on and scan the far side before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Switch target moves too close to the centre
commonErrors.correction: Hold width to stretch the defensive shape.

commonErrors.error: Players remain stationary after disposal
commonErrors.correction: Follow the football and support the next possession.

commonErrors.error: Ball movement is too slow
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the next kick before receiving.

progressions: Allow defenders to adjust their positioning.
Add moving switch and outlet targets.
Continue into a live transition game.
successIndicators: Complete the switch before pressure recovers.
matchApplication: This drill replicates defensive ball movement when: One boundary is congested. The opposition has shifted across. A central release player is available. The open side can be accessed. A direct clearance would create a turnover risk.
