KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Switch, Run and Receive
primarySkill: Following a Switch to Receive Again
objective: Develop the ability to switch the football and immediately support the next phase of play. Players learn that a kick does not end their involvement and practise running to receive again in a new position.
players:
Minimum: 8
Ideal: 12–20
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create four positions in a wide diamond:
• Starting player.
• Central release.
• Wide switch target.
• Forward return target.
• Place the starting player and central release approximately 15 metres apart.
• Place the switch target 20–25 metres across the ground.
• Place the return target 15–20 metres ahead of the switch target.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to the central release.
2. Player A immediately begins a hard support run across and forward.
3. The central release marks and kicks to the wide switch target.
4. The switch target marks and looks inside.
5. Player A continues the support run into the return lane.
6. The switch target kicks to Player A.
7. Player A marks and delivers to the forward target.
8. Players rotate through each position.
9. Repeat in both directions.
10. The original kicker must time the support run so they arrive after the switch has been completed.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Move immediately after disposal.
Run with purpose rather than jogging.
Maintain a clear support angle.
Communicate during the run.
Scan while moving.
Kick to the runner’s advantage.
Avoid arriving too early and becoming stationary.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the runner arrives in space.

commonErrors.error: Original kicker watches the play
commonErrors.correction: Begin the support run immediately after disposal.

commonErrors.error: Runner arrives too early
commonErrors.correction: Delay slightly or use a wider running line.

commonErrors.error: Support angle is too narrow
commonErrors.correction: Run across and forward into clear space.

commonErrors.error: Switch player does not scan inside
commonErrors.correction: Look for the returning runner before marking.

commonErrors.error: Final kick is rushed due to fatigue
commonErrors.correction: Control the final steps and maintain technique.

progressions: Add a second possible returning runner.
Add a time target for completing the chain.
Finish with a shot at goal.
successIndicators: Maintain kicking quality under physical load.
matchApplication: This drill develops repeat involvement during: Defensive switches. Half-back overlaps. Wing transitions. Give-and-go ball movement. Attacking chains through the corridor.
relatedDrills: KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Corridor Transfer Kick
primarySkill: Transferring the Football into the Corridor
objective: Develop the ability to move the football from a wide position into a central corridor target. Players learn to recognise when the central option is available and deliver a firm, accurate kick that supports continued forward movement.
players:
Minimum: 8
Ideal: 12–20
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one wide ball-carrier position near a boundary.
• Create a corridor gate approximately four to six metres wide, 20–25 metres infield.
• Position a central receiver beyond the gate.
• Place a forward target another 20 metres ahead.
• A passive defender begins near the corridor gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The wide ball carrier receives from a feeder.
2. The central receiver presents through the corridor gate.
3. The defender moves to either partially close or leave the corridor lane.
4. The ball carrier scans the defender and central receiver.
5. When the lane is available, the ball carrier kicks firmly through the gate.
6. The central receiver marks and turns forward.
7. The central receiver kicks to the forward target.
8. Players rotate positions.
9. If the corridor is closed, the ball carrier uses a designated safe outlet before the drill resets.
10. The drill should reward correct recognition rather than forcing every kick into the corridor.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the central lane early.
Recognise whether the corridor is open.
Avoid forcing the kick when pressure has closed the lane.
Use a firm, direct trajectory.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Prepare the central receiver to turn forward.
Maintain width when the corridor is unavailable.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Scanning by the wide ball carrier.
Decision to use or avoid the corridor.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier forces the corridor when closed
commonErrors.correction: Use the safe outlet and wait for a better opportunity.

commonErrors.error: Kick floats through the central lane
commonErrors.correction: Use a firmer, flatter trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Central receiver stands still
commonErrors.correction: Present actively through the gate.

commonErrors.error: Receiver marks with back to the forward target
commonErrors.correction: Position side-on and scan before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Player ignores an open corridor
commonErrors.correction: Scan centrally before looking down the boundary.

progressions: Use moving central and forward targets.
Continue into live play after the central mark.
regressions: Predetermine whether the lane is open.
successIndicators: Prepare the central receiver to continue forward.
matchApplication: Corridor transfer kicks can: Open the ground. Create faster forward movement. Move behind defensive pressure. Improve scoring opportunities. Change the point of attack.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick

title: Three-Kick Transition Chain
objective: Develop the ability to connect three consecutive kicks while moving the football from defence into attack. Players learn to prepare before receiving, maintain spacing and support the possession chain after disposal.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create four stations extending from defence towards attack:
• Station A: Defensive start.
• Station B: Short outlet.
• Station C: Wide or central transition target.
• Station D: Forward target.
• Place each station 15–25 metres apart.
• Players form lines at all stations.
• Use a second football once the group understands the pattern.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to Player B.
2. Player A follows the disposal.
3. Player B scans, marks and turns towards Player C.
4. Player B kicks to Player C and follows.
5. Player C marks while moving or plays on immediately.
6. Player C kicks to Player D.
7. Player D marks and carries the football back along the outside of the drill.
8. All players rotate forward one station.
9. Continue for the allocated time.
10. Reverse the direction or change station angles.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the next target before receiving.
Communicate early.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Follow every disposal.
Maintain width and spacing.
Move the football quickly without rushing.
Adjust kicking weight for each distance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the second football creates congestion.

commonErrors.error: Receiver watches only the incoming football
commonErrors.correction: Scan the next target before completing the mark.

commonErrors.error: Players remain stationary after kicking
commonErrors.correction: Follow the disposal and support the chain.

commonErrors.error: Kicks arrive behind moving receivers
commonErrors.correction: Place the football into their path.

commonErrors.error: Lines become congested
commonErrors.correction: Increase station spacing or reduce football numbers.

commonErrors.error: Players rush to complete the chain
commonErrors.correction: Maintain technical quality before increasing speed.

progressions: Introduce moving targets at every station.
Add a decision between two targets.
Require non-preferred foot use at one station.
Finish with a shot at goal.
regressions: Walk through the pattern before increasing pace.
successIndicators: Maintain accuracy under increasing physical load.
matchApplication: This drill replicates transition ball movement through: Defensive exit. Half-back connection. Wing or corridor movement. Forward entry. Repeated support running.

title: Boundary-to-Corridor Transition
primarySkill: Moving the Football from Boundary to Corridor
objective: Develop the ability to move possession from a wide boundary position into the corridor through a controlled sequence of kicks. Players learn to recognise the correct moment to transfer infield and continue the transition forward.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create four stations:
• Boundary starting position.
• Short boundary outlet.
• Central corridor receiver.
• Forward target.
• Place the boundary outlet 15–20 metres ahead of the starting position.
• Place the corridor receiver 20–25 metres infield from the boundary outlet.
• Place the forward target another 20–30 metres ahead.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A begins with the football near the boundary.
2. Player A kicks to Player B at the short boundary outlet.
3. Player B scans the corridor before marking.
4. The passive defender adjusts position to either open or partially close the corridor.
5. If the corridor is open, Player B kicks to Player C infield.
6. Player C marks, turns forward and kicks to Player D.
7. If the corridor is closed, Player B uses a designated safe return option before the drill resets.
8. Players follow their disposals and rotate.
9. Repeat from both boundaries.
10. The drill should reward recognition rather than forcing the corridor kick every time.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Maintain width on the boundary.
Scan infield before receiving.
Recognise whether the corridor is open.
Use a firm, accurate transfer kick.
Avoid floating the football into pressure.
Position the corridor receiver side-on.
Turn forward immediately after the central mark.

commonErrors.error: Player forces the corridor when closed
commonErrors.correction: Use the safe option and retain possession.

commonErrors.error: Corridor receiver stands directly behind the defender
commonErrors.correction: Move into a clear diagonal passing lane.

commonErrors.error: Transfer kick floats
commonErrors.correction: Use a firmer and flatter trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Boundary player receives with no awareness
commonErrors.correction: Scan infield before the mark.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal
commonErrors.correction: Follow the football and support the next phase.

regressions: Predetermine when the corridor is open.
successIndicators: Continue forward after entering the corridor.
matchApplication: This drill applies when teams: Exit defence along the boundary. Draw opponents towards one side. Transfer into the corridor. Create a more direct route to goal. Change from safe possession to attacking transition.

title: Corridor-to-Forward Entry
objective: Develop the ability to deliver an effective forward entry after receiving possession in the corridor. Players learn to scan multiple forward options, recognise space and kick to the leading player’s advantage.
players:
Minimum: 9
Ideal: 12–21
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one corridor receiving position approximately 45–60 metres from goal or a designated scoring zone.
• Create three forward starting positions:
• Left lead.
• Central lead.
• Right lead.
• Position one passive defender between the corridor player and the forwards.
• A feeder stands 15 metres behind the corridor receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The corridor player scans all three forward positions.
2. The feeder kicks to the corridor player.
3. As the football travels, the forwards begin their leads.
4. The defender moves to influence one of the options.
5. The corridor player marks, assesses the available space and selects a target.
6. The corridor player kicks to the chosen forward’s advantage.
7. The forward marks or gathers and completes a shot at goal or target kick.
8. Players rotate through corridor, forward, defender and feeder roles.
9. Continue for the allocated time.
10. The forward entries should vary rather than follow a fixed sequence.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before receiving.
Identify forward spacing.
Avoid kicking to crowded areas.
Use the lead that creates the greatest separation.
Place the football into the receiver’s path.
Use a lower trajectory when the lane is clear.
Avoid overkicking the leading player.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing and spacing of forward leads.
Whether forwards lead into the same space.

commonErrors.error: All forwards lead to the same area
commonErrors.correction: Allocate different starting lanes and lead patterns.

commonErrors.error: Corridor player kicks to the loudest target
commonErrors.correction: Select the option with the best space and separation.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes over the forward’s head
commonErrors.correction: Reduce power and improve touch.

commonErrors.error: Player waits too long after marking
commonErrors.correction: Make the decision while the leads are developing.

commonErrors.error: Kick is placed directly at the defender
commonErrors.correction: Deliver into the open side of the lead.

progressions: Allow forwards to choose their own leads.
matchApplication: This drill replicates attacking possessions when players: Win the football through the corridor. Break a defensive line. Deliver inside 50. Select between several forward targets. Need to avoid an intercept defender.

title: Inside-50 Target Selection
objective: Develop the ability to select the most effective target when entering the forward 50. Players learn to compare multiple options, recognise dangerous space and avoid kicking automatically to a crowded contest.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create one ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
• Set three forward options:
• Short lead.
• Deep lead.
• Lateral lead into space.
• Position two passive defenders to influence the available options.
• A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
• Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier scans the forward structure.
2. The feeder delivers the football.
3. As the ball carrier receives, the three forwards begin different leads.
4. The defenders adjust to cover or influence selected options.
5. The ball carrier chooses the target that offers:
6. The greatest separation.
7. The safest kicking lane.
8. The strongest scoring opportunity.
9. The ball carrier delivers the football.
10. The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before possession.
Recognise the deepest dangerous option.
Use short leads when deep space is unavailable.
Avoid kicking to outnumbered contests.
Consider the defender’s position.
Kick to the forward’s advantage.
Maintain composure around forward 50.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players repeatedly choose the deepest option.
Whether decisions create realistic shots at goal.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier bombs to a crowded area
commonErrors.correction: Scan for short and lateral options.

commonErrors.error: Player chooses the first lead seen
commonErrors.correction: Compare all available options before committing.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead into the same lane
commonErrors.correction: Maintain distinct leading patterns.

commonErrors.error: Kick favours the defender
commonErrors.correction: Place the football on the forward’s protected side.

commonErrors.error: Player becomes rushed near forward 50
commonErrors.correction: Stay composed and use the best available option.

progressions: Continue into live play after the entry.
matchApplication: This drill develops decision making during one of the most important moments in Australian Football: the kick inside 50. It applies to: Fast entries. Slow possession entries. Entries from the corridor. Entries from the boundary. Rebound and turnover situations.
relatedDrills: KK-052 – Deep versus Short Entry Decision

title: Forward Entry to Space
objective: Develop the ability to kick into open forward space so a teammate can attack the football at speed. Players learn to place the ball away from defenders and avoid kicking directly to a stationary target.
players:
Minimum: 8
Ideal: 12–20
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one ball-carrier position 40–55 metres from goal or a target area.
• Create three forward-entry zones:
• Left pocket space.
• Central space.
• Right pocket space.
• A forward begins behind the zones.
• A passive defender begins between the forward and ball carrier.
• A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier receives from the feeder.
2. The forward observes the defender’s position.
3. The forward leads towards the open target zone.
4. The ball carrier reads the lead.
5. The ball carrier kicks into the selected space.
6. The forward attacks the football at speed.
7. The forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
8. Players rotate roles.
9. Continue from different entry angles.
10. The football should be placed into space rather than directly onto the forward’s head unless the lead demands it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Read the defender’s position.
Kick away from defensive pressure.
Use space in front of the forward.
Match kicking weight to the lead.
Keep the ball low enough to reduce defensive recovery time.
Avoid overkicking the target zone.
Allow the forward to maintain speed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the football remains inside the target area.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier kicks directly at the forward
commonErrors.correction: Place the football into the open space ahead.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes too close to the defender
commonErrors.correction: Target the forward’s protected side.

commonErrors.error: Football carries beyond the zone
commonErrors.correction: Reduce power and improve touch.

commonErrors.error: Forward waits for the football
commonErrors.correction: Attack the target zone at speed.

commonErrors.error: Kick is too high
commonErrors.correction: Use a flatter trajectory where the lane is clear.

progressions: Allow the forward to choose any zone.
successIndicators: Allow the forward to maintain speed.
matchApplication: Kicking to forward space is especially valuable when: The forward line is open. Defenders are positioned goal side. A teammate has speed advantage. Direct marking targets are unavailable. The team is attacking from turnover.
relatedDrills: KK-052 – Deep versus Short Entry Decision

title: Lowered-Eyes Forward Entry
objective: Develop the habit of lowering the eyes before entering forward 50 and identifying short or lateral targets rather than automatically kicking long to a contest.
players:
Minimum: 9
Ideal: 12–21
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place the ball carrier outside forward 50.
• Create:
• One deep forward target.
• Two short lead targets.
• One lateral target.
• Position one or two passive defenders near the deep option.
• A feeder stands 15 metres behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier scans the forward line before receiving.
2. The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
3. The deep forward and short targets begin their movements.
4. The defenders influence the deep option.
5. The ball carrier lowers the eyes and assesses the shorter targets.
6. The ball carrier selects the best available option.
7. The receiver marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
8. Players rotate through all roles.
9. Continue with different defensive positions.
10. The deep option remains available when it is genuinely the best choice.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan deep and short.
Avoid becoming fixed on the goal square.
Recognise defenders dropping back.
Reward short leads with separation.
Use controlled kicking weight.
Place the football in front of the receiver.
Remain patient while moving at speed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player scans short options.
Whether the player defaults to the deep kick.
Quality of the resulting scoring chance.

commonErrors.error: Player automatically kicks long
commonErrors.correction: Scan short targets before beginning the kicking action.

commonErrors.error: Short forwards lead too late
commonErrors.correction: Begin the lead as the ball carrier receives.

commonErrors.error: Kick is too powerful for the short target
commonErrors.correction: Reduce force and use touch.

commonErrors.error: Player ignores an open lateral target
commonErrors.correction: Scan the full width of the forward line.

commonErrors.error: Deep target is used despite an outnumber
commonErrors.correction: Select the free short option.

progressions: Add a closing defender behind the ball carrier.
Allow defenders to cover short options.
regressions: Use one short and one deep target.
matchApplication: Lowered-eyes entries are important when: Defenders drop deep. The goal square is crowded. Short forwards create separation. A lateral option improves the scoring angle. Controlled possession is preferable to a contest.
relatedDrills: KK-052 – Deep versus Short Entry Decision
KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure

title: Deep versus Short Entry Decision
primarySkill: Choosing Between Deep and Short Forward Entries
objective: Develop the ability to compare a deep attacking option with a shorter possession option and select the entry that creates the strongest scoring opportunity.
players:
Minimum: 9
Ideal: 12–21
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create:
• One ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
• One deep forward starting near goal.
• One short forward starting 25–35 metres from goal.
• One defender assigned to influence the deep option.
• One second defender positioned between the short and deep areas.
• A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier scans both forward options.
2. The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
3. The deep and short forwards begin their leads.
4. The defenders adjust their positioning.
5. The ball carrier assesses:
6. Separation.
7. Defender numbers.
8. Kicking lane.
9. Likely scoring outcome.
10. The ball carrier selects either the deep or short option.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before possession.
Compare the quality of both options.
Use the deep target when separation is clear.
Use the short option when defenders protect space behind.
Consider the likely shot location.
Avoid choosing by habit.
Weight each kick appropriately.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player repeatedly chooses one option.
Quality of the resulting shot at goal.

commonErrors.error: Player always chooses the deep target
commonErrors.correction: Compare defensive numbers and short separation.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier always chooses the easy short kick
commonErrors.correction: Use the deep option when it creates a stronger scoring chance.

commonErrors.error: Decision is made before defenders move
commonErrors.correction: Continue scanning as the leads develop.

commonErrors.error: Kick weight does not suit the selected target
commonErrors.correction: Adjust trajectory and power to the distance.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead into overlapping space
commonErrors.correction: Separate the deep and short leading lanes.

matchApplication: This drill develops forward-entry decisions when: A deep forward has separation. Defenders drop behind the ball. A short lead presents inside 50. The ball carrier must choose between territory and possession. The quality of the next shot matters more than distance gained.
relatedDrills: KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure
KK-054 – Forward Entry with Closing Defender

title: Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure
objective: Develop the ability to deliver an effective forward entry while a defender applies pressure from behind. Players learn to accelerate into space, scan the forward line early and complete the kick before pressure forces a rushed disposal.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place:
• One ball-carrier starting cone 55–65 metres from goal.
• One chasing defender’s cone three to five metres behind.
• Three forward starting positions inside 50.
• Optional left, central and right target zones.
• The ball carrier begins with the football.
• The forwards begin in separate leading lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. On the coach’s signal, the ball carrier and chasing defender begin.
2. The ball carrier accelerates towards forward 50.
3. The forwards begin their leads.
4. The ball carrier scans the available targets while running.
5. The defender closes from behind without tackling.
6. The ball carrier selects the best option and delivers before the defender reaches effective pressure.
7. The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
8. Players rotate through ball-carrier, defender and forward roles.
9. Adjust the defender’s starting gap to suit the group.
10. The ball carrier should not wait until reaching the 50-metre line if a strong option appears earlier.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Accelerate immediately.
Keep the eyes forward.
Scan before entering kicking range.
Prepare the football before the defender closes.
Recognise the first strong forward option.
Avoid looking backwards repeatedly.
Maintain balance through the final steps.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the defender maintains safe pressure.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier looks backwards repeatedly
commonErrors.correction: Trust the starting gap and scan the forward line.

commonErrors.error: Player waits too long to kick
commonErrors.correction: Use the first strong forward option.

commonErrors.error: Ball preparation begins after pressure arrives
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the football earlier in the run.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes directly to the defender’s side of the forward
commonErrors.correction: Place it on the protected side.

commonErrors.error: Kicker loses balance at maximum speed
commonErrors.correction: Control the final steps before disposal.

progressions: Allow controlled tackling before the kicking line.
successIndicators: Prepare the football before pressure arrives.
matchApplication: This drill applies when players: Break from congestion. Receive an overlap handball. Attack from turnover. Carry through the corridor. Enter forward 50 under recovery pressure.
relatedDrills: KK-054 – Forward Entry with Closing Defender

title: Forward Entry with Closing Defender
objective: Develop the ability to create and use a forward-entry kicking lane while a defender closes from the front. Players learn to recognise the defender’s line, make a small angle change and deliver into the forward 50 without kicking into smothering pressure.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place:
• One ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
• One closing defender 10–12 metres ahead.
• Two forward-entry gates, one left and one right of the defender.
• One forward target beyond each gate.
• One feeder behind the ball carrier.
• Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
2. The defender closes from the front with hands raised.
3. The forwards begin leads through the two entry gates.
4. The ball carrier scans the defender and forward options.
5. The ball carrier moves slightly off the defender’s line.
6. The ball carrier delivers through the clearer gate.
7. The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
8. Players rotate through all roles.
9. Vary defender closing angles.
10. The defender pressures the lane without making unsafe contact.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan both entry lanes before receiving.
Recognise the defender’s closing line.
Use a small lateral movement.
Prepare the football early.
Avoid drifting too far sideways.
Select the forward away from pressure.
Maintain a compact and balanced kick.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks directly into the defender
commonErrors.correction: Move off the closing line before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Attacker makes an excessive sideways run
commonErrors.correction: Use only the angle required to create the lane.

commonErrors.error: Ball preparation starts too late
commonErrors.correction: Prepare as the defender begins closing.

commonErrors.error: Player chooses the pressured forward
commonErrors.correction: Select the lead away from the defender’s movement.

commonErrors.error: Defender enters the kicking-leg area
commonErrors.correction: Increase spacing and reinforce controlled pressure.

matchApplication: This drill applies when players: Exit a stoppage towards forward 50. Receive in the corridor. Approach a high defender. Enter forward 50 under frontal pressure. Need to avoid an intercept or smother.
relatedDrills: KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure

title: Forward Entry After Evasion
primarySkill: Forward Entry After Beating an Opponent
objective: Develop the ability to evade an opponent before delivering accurately inside 50. Players learn to use the evasive movement to create time and a better kicking angle rather than rushing immediately after beating the defender.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place:
• One attacker’s starting cone outside forward 50.
• One evasion defender eight metres ahead.
• Two exit gates around the defender.
• Three forward leading lanes beyond the exit gates.
• One feeder behind the attacker.
• Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder passes to the attacker.
2. The attacker moves towards the evasion defender.
3. The defender shades one side.
4. The attacker uses a sidestep, baulk or change of pace to exit through the opposite gate.
5. The forwards begin their leads.
6. The attacker accelerates out of the evasion.
7. The attacker scans and delivers to the best available forward.
8. The selected forward finishes at goal.
9. Players rotate through all roles.
10. Vary the defender’s positioning and forward leads.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Read the defender.
Protect the football during the evasion.
Use decisive footwork.
Accelerate out of the move.
Lift the eyes immediately after escaping.
Regain body alignment.
Select the best lead.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes after evading.

commonErrors.error: Attacker watches the football after the evasion
commonErrors.correction: Lift the eyes immediately and scan forward.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks while drifting sideways
commonErrors.correction: Straighten and regain balance first.

commonErrors.error: Evasion is too wide
commonErrors.correction: Use a more direct movement through the exit gate.

commonErrors.error: Player beats the defender but delays too long
commonErrors.correction: Use the space immediately.

commonErrors.error: Forward leads begin before the attacker escapes
commonErrors.correction: Time leads to the moment the attacker creates space.

progressions: Reduce the size of exit gates.
regressions: Replace the defender with a pole.
Allow the attacker to stop after evading.
matchApplication: This drill applies when players: Beat a midfielder at the top of forward 50. Step around a high defender. Escape congestion. Create a better forward-entry angle. Turn a pressured possession into an attacking opportunity.
relatedDrills: KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure
KK-054 – Forward Entry with Closing Defender
KK-056 – Forward Entry After Ground Ball

title: Forward Entry After Ground Ball
primarySkill: Forward Entry After a Ground Ball Gather
objective: Develop the ability to gather a loose football outside forward 50 and quickly convert possession into an effective forward entry. Players learn to secure the football first, accelerate from the contest and identify the best attacking option.
players:
Minimum: 9
Ideal: 12–21
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place:
• One starting cone 55 metres from goal.
• One ground-ball collection zone eight metres ahead.
• Three forward starting positions inside 50.
• One feeder beside the collection zone.
• Players form lines at the starting and forward positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacker runs towards the collection zone.
2. The feeder rolls the football into the attacker’s path.
3. The attacker gathers cleanly.
4. The attacker accelerates away from the collection point.
5. The forwards begin their leads.
6. The attacker scans and selects the best option.
7. The attacker delivers inside 50.
8. The forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
9. Players rotate through all positions.
10. Vary the ground-ball angle and forward leads.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Approach under control.
Get low and use two hands.
Secure possession before accelerating.
Take the first steps away from the collection point.
Lift the eyes early after the gather.
Prepare the football during the run.
Select the forward with the best space.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes immediately after gathering.

commonErrors.error: Player looks forward before securing the ball
commonErrors.correction: Complete the gather first.

commonErrors.error: Attacker remains low for too long
commonErrors.correction: Rise and accelerate after possession is secure.

commonErrors.error: Ball preparation begins too late
commonErrors.correction: Move it into kicking position during the exit steps.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks to the first voice heard
commonErrors.correction: Scan all forward options.

commonErrors.error: Technique collapses after a poor gather
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance before disposal.

regressions: Allow the player to stop after gathering.
matchApplication: This drill applies when players: Win a loose ball outside forward 50. Gather a spill from a contest. Recover a turnover. Crumb a marking contest. Attack before the opposition can reset.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick
KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure
KK-057 – Forward Entry After Handball Receive

title: Forward Entry After Handball Receive
primarySkill: Forward Entry After an Overlap Handball
objective: Develop the ability to receive a handball at speed outside forward 50 and deliver accurately to a leading forward. Players learn to time the support run, receive in front and prepare the football without losing momentum.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create:
• One initial ball carrier outside forward 50.
• One support runner starting behind and to the side.
• Three forward leading positions.
• One feeder or starting line.
• The initial ball carrier begins with the football.
• The support runner starts three to five metres behind.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier begins moving towards forward 50.
2. The support runner delays, then accelerates past.
3. The support runner calls for the football.
4. The ball carrier handballs into the runner’s path.
5. The forwards begin their leads.
6. The support runner receives without slowing.
7. The support runner scans and delivers to the best forward option.
8. The selected forward finishes at goal.
9. Players rotate through all roles.
10. Repeat from both sides.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Delay the support run.
Accelerate past the ball carrier.
Communicate early.
Receive in front of the body.
Scan the forward line before and during the receive.
Prepare the football immediately.
Control the final steps.

commonErrors.error: Support runner leaves too early
commonErrors.correction: Delay until the ball carrier begins moving.

commonErrors.error: Handball goes behind the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Place it into the runner’s path.

commonErrors.error: Runner watches only the handball
commonErrors.correction: Scan forward before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Player rushes the kick immediately after receiving
commonErrors.correction: Control the final steps.

commonErrors.error: Forwards begin leading too early
commonErrors.correction: Time the leads to the overlap receive.

progressions: Allow the ball carrier to choose whether to handball.
regressions: Allow the receiver to stop before kicking.
matchApplication: This drill applies when players: Create an overlap through the middle. Receive a release handball. Break the defensive line. Enter forward 50 at speed. Deliver before defenders can recover.
relatedDrills: KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure

title: Forward Entry from Boundary
primarySkill: Forward Entry from a Wide Angle
objective: Develop the ability to enter forward 50 effectively from near the boundary. Players learn to assess central, short and deep options while avoiding predictable kicks directly down the line.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one ball-carrier position near the boundary outside forward 50.
• Create three forward targets:
• Short lead along the boundary.
• Central lead into the corridor side of forward 50.
• Deep lead towards goal.
• Position one passive defender to influence the central lane and another near the deep option.
• A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier scans all forward targets.
2. The feeder delivers the football.
3. The forwards begin their leads.
4. The defenders adjust their positioning.
5. The ball carrier selects the best available entry.
6. The ball carrier delivers to the receiver’s advantage.
7. The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
8. Players rotate through all roles.
9. Repeat from both boundaries.
10. The central option should be used when available, but not forced.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan inside before defaulting down the line.
Recognise boundary restrictions.
Open the hips towards central targets.
Use the short option if deep space is crowded.
Kick away from defenders.
Adjust trajectory for the selected lead.
Avoid overkicking narrow angles.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Quality of the resulting scoring chance.

commonErrors.error: Player automatically kicks down the boundary
commonErrors.correction: Scan central and short options first.

commonErrors.error: Kicker closes the body towards the line
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the intended target.

commonErrors.error: Central kick floats
commonErrors.correction: Use a firmer trajectory through the lane.

commonErrors.error: Deep option is selected despite an outnumber
commonErrors.correction: Use the short or central target.

commonErrors.error: Player steps out of bounds
commonErrors.correction: Reduce foot movement and maintain line awareness.

progressions: Add a player on the mark.
regressions: Allow the player to begin stationary with the football.
successIndicators: Scan inside and down the line.
matchApplication: This drill applies when players: Enter forward 50 from the wing. Possess near the boundary. Need to avoid a crowded deep contest. Access a central forward. Use a short lead to improve the scoring angle.
relatedDrills: KK-052 – Deep versus Short Entry Decision
KK-057 – Forward Entry After Handball Receive
KK-059 – Forward Entry from Opposite Foot

title: Forward Entry from Opposite Foot
objective: Develop the ability to deliver inside 50 using the non-preferred foot when body position, pressure or field location removes the preferred-side option.
players:
Minimum: 8
Ideal: 12–20
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
• Create two leading targets positioned so the non-preferred foot provides the more natural kicking angle.
• A feeder stands 10–15 metres behind or beside the ball carrier.
• Players rotate through feeder, kicker and forward roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker receives from the feeder.
2. The forwards begin their leads.
3. The kicker must use the non-preferred foot.
4. The kicker selects the better of the two targets.
5. The kicker delivers to the receiver’s advantage.
6. The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
7. Players rotate positions.
8. Repeat from both sides of the ground.
9. Keep the distance realistic enough for sound technique.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Hold the football correctly for the non-preferred side.
Guide it directly over the kicking foot.
Maintain balance.
Use a smooth leg swing.
Accept reduced distance.
Select a target within realistic range.
Avoid turning back onto the preferred foot automatically.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Willingness to use the non-preferred foot.
Whether players turn back into pressure.

commonErrors.error: Player turns back onto the preferred foot
commonErrors.correction: Commit to the non-preferred-side option.

commonErrors.error: Ball crosses the body
commonErrors.correction: Hold and guide it directly over the kicking foot.

commonErrors.error: Player tries to kick too far
commonErrors.correction: Choose a closer target and prioritise contact.

commonErrors.error: Kicker falls sideways
commonErrors.correction: Slow the approach and finish balanced.

commonErrors.error: Decision is delayed through lack of confidence
commonErrors.correction: Scan early and commit once the option appears.

progressions: Add passive pressure on the preferred side.
regressions: Return to basic non-preferred foot kicking.
matchApplication: Non-preferred foot forward entries are required when: Opponents block the preferred side. Players receive near the boundary. Body position limits turning. Fast ball movement demands immediate disposal. A teammate is open on the opposite angle.
relatedDrills: KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure

title: Forward Entry Decision Game
objective: Develop live forward-entry decisions in a constrained game. Players learn to select between leading targets, space, short possession and deeper options while defenders actively influence the available lanes.
players:
Minimum: 12
Ideal: 16–24
Maximum: 30 using two areas
setup:
• Create a playing area extending from approximately 70 metres from goal to the goal line.
• Divide players into:
• Attacking team.
• Defending team.
• Optional neutral transition players.
• Recommended starting format:
• Four to six attackers.
• Three to five defenders.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacking team gains possession outside forward 50.
2. Forwards create leads and maintain spacing.
3. Defenders attempt to deny the most dangerous options.
4. The ball carrier decides whether to:
5. Kick to a leading forward.
6. Kick into space.
7. Use a short possession.
8. Switch the angle.
9. Retain the football.
10. The attack continues until:
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before receiving.
Maintain forward spacing.
Avoid leading into the same area.
Recognise defender numbers.
Use the first strong option.
Avoid low-percentage kicks to outnumbered contests.
Kick to space when appropriate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players retain possession when required.

commonErrors.error: Forwards crowd one area
commonErrors.correction: Maintain separate leading lanes and depth.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier automatically kicks long
commonErrors.correction: Scan short, lateral and space options.

commonErrors.error: Attackers hold the football too long
commonErrors.correction: Use the first strong option before defenders recover.

commonErrors.error: Players force kicks into outnumbers
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession or change the angle.

commonErrors.error: Entries favour defenders
commonErrors.correction: Kick to the forward’s protected side or into open space.

progressions: Add transition after a defensive turnover.
Restrict the number of possessions before entry.
regressions: Stop after the first forward entry.
matchApplication: This drill directly replicates live inside-50 decision making, including: Fast entries. Slow entries. Boundary entries. Corridor entries. Kicks to space. Short possession. Deep contests. Entries under pressure.
relatedDrills: KK-052 – Deep versus Short Entry Decision
KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure

title: Short Kick Retention
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession using short, accurate kicks. Players learn to control the weight and trajectory of the football so the receiver can mark cleanly and continue the possession chain.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize: Small to Medium Area Approximately 30 m × 25 m
setup:
• Create four stations in a square or diamond.
• Recommended spacing:
• Under 10–12: 10–12 metres.
• Under 14 and above: 15–20 metres.
• Place two to four players at each station.
• Begin with one football.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to Player B at the next station.
2. Player B marks the football.
3. Player A follows the kick to the back of Player B’s line.
4. Player B turns and kicks to Player C.
5. The pattern continues around the area.
6. Change direction after several minutes.
7. Add a second football once players maintain accuracy and spacing.
8. Every kick should travel a realistic short-marking distance for the age group.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Kick to the receiver’s chest or advantage.
Control the power of the kick.
Use a flatter trajectory.
Communicate before disposal.
Present clear hands.
Follow the football.
Avoid kicking too hard at short range.

commonErrors.error: Kick arrives too hard
commonErrors.correction: Reduce leg speed and use more touch.

commonErrors.error: Football floats slowly
commonErrors.correction: Use a firmer, flatter trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Receiver waits flat-footed
commonErrors.correction: Present towards the kicker with visible hands.

commonErrors.error: Player watches the kick and does not rotate
commonErrors.correction: Follow the disposal immediately.

commonErrors.error: Kicks repeatedly fall short
commonErrors.correction: Complete the follow-through towards the target.

progressions: Add a passive defender in the centre.
Introduce a time target for completing a circuit.
regressions: Allow players to handball through the pattern first.
successIndicators: Retain possession through the full circuit.
matchApplication: Short kicks are used to: Retain possession. Move around defensive zones. Exit defence safely. Control tempo. Find uncontested teammates. Improve the angle of the next disposal.

title: Short Kick and Reposition
objective: Develop the ability to complete a short kick and immediately reposition to support the next possession. Players learn to create a new passing option instead of remaining where the original disposal was made.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three main passing stations in a triangle.
• Place one support cone approximately five to eight metres away from each passing station.
• Players form lines at the three main stations.
• The football begins at one station.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to Player B.
2. Player A immediately runs to the nearby support cone.
3. Player B marks and turns towards Player C.
4. Player B kicks to Player C.
5. Player B runs to their support cone.
6. Player C may kick to the repositioned Player A rather than continuing directly around the triangle.
7. Players continue moving between main and support positions.
8. Rotate the direction after several minutes.
9. The drill should create repeated short options rather than a fixed circular pattern.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Move immediately after kicking.
Reposition into visible space.
Avoid running behind the player with the football.
Maintain a useful passing angle.
Communicate while moving.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Avoid standing on the same line as another target.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players become hidden behind others.
Whether players stop once reaching a cone.

commonErrors.error: Player remains stationary after kicking
commonErrors.correction: Move immediately to the support cone.

commonErrors.error: Repositioned player runs behind the ball carrier
commonErrors.correction: Move into a visible side angle.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd the same area
commonErrors.correction: Maintain separation between support options.

commonErrors.error: Kicker delivers before the receiver is ready
commonErrors.correction: Require eye contact or voice before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players stand still at support cones
commonErrors.correction: Continue adjusting to remain available.

progressions: Convert into a live keepings-off game.
regressions: Pause and reset after every three kicks.
matchApplication: Players must reposition after kicking to: Create a return option. Support a switch. Provide an outlet. Maintain possession. Prevent the ball carrier becoming isolated.

title: Possession Triangle
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession through short angled kicks. Players learn to create passing lanes, receive side-on and move the football away from pressure.
groundSize: Small to Medium Area Approximately 25 m × 25 m
setup:
• Place three cones in a triangle.
• Position one support cone between each main cone and slightly inside the triangle.
• Players form lines at the three outside cones.
• The football begins at one outside cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to Player B at the next outside cone.
2. Player A moves to the nearby support cone.
3. Player B scans before marking.
4. Player B may kick:
5. Directly to Player C.
6. Back to Player A at the support cone.
7. The receiving player continues the possession.
8. All players move after disposal.
9. Change direction after several minutes.
10. The coach may initially nominate the option before allowing players to decide.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan both direct and support options.
Receive side-on.
Use a short, firm kick.
Move after disposal.
Maintain triangular spacing.
Avoid standing behind a defender or teammate.
Use the safer option when the direct lane is closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players force the direct kick.

commonErrors.error: Players collapse into a straight line
commonErrors.correction: Maintain triangular spacing.

commonErrors.error: Receiver does not scan support
commonErrors.correction: Check both options before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: Kick is floated
commonErrors.correction: Use a firmer short pass.

commonErrors.error: Support player stands behind the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Move to a visible angle.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier forces the direct lane
commonErrors.correction: Use the support option when required.

regressions: Allow players to walk through the pattern.
matchApplication: Triangular support structures help teams: Retain possession. Move around defenders. Create safer kicking angles. Switch play. Support the ball carrier.

title: Short Kick Keepings-Off
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession using short kicks while a defender pressures the available passing lanes. Players learn to move into space, select safe options and avoid predictable disposals.
setup:
• Create a rectangular playing area.
• Recommended formats:
• Four attackers versus one defender.
• Five attackers versus two defenders.
• Attackers spread around the outside and inside of the area.
• Defenders begin centrally.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Attackers retain possession using kicks only.
2. The player with the football may not run more than several steps.
3. Defenders attempt to intercept or spoil.
4. After a mark, the receiver has a limited time to dispose.
5. Attackers score one point for every five completed kicks.
6. If defenders win possession, rotate the player responsible for the turnover into defence.
7. Continue for timed blocks.
8. The coach may allow handball as a regression.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Spread immediately.
Create short diagonal options.
Scan before receiving.
Avoid standing directly behind defenders.
Kick away from pressure.
Use the safest effective option.
Move again after disposal.

commonErrors.error: Attackers crowd around the football
commonErrors.correction: Spread to the full width and depth of the area.

commonErrors.error: Players hide behind defenders
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally to create a visible passing lane.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier holds possession too long
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the next option before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Short kicks are too high
commonErrors.correction: Use a flatter trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal
commonErrors.correction: Reposition immediately.

progressions: Remove stationary marks and require continuous play.
matchApplication: This drill develops possession control when teams need to: Slow the game. Maintain the football. Move around a defensive zone. protect a lead. Create a better attacking angle.
relatedDrills: KK-066 – Possession Kick with End Zones

title: Three-versus-One Kicking Possession
objective: Develop the ability to use a three-versus-one advantage to retain possession and move the football past a defender. Players learn to maintain width, draw pressure and release to the free target.
players:
Minimum: 4
Ideal: 8–16 using multiple groups
Maximum: 20
groundSize: Small Area Approximately 20 m × 15 m per group
setup:
• Create a rectangular area.
• Place three attackers around the outside edges.
• Position one defender inside the area.
• One attacker begins with the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The three attackers retain possession using kicks.
2. The defender pressures the ball carrier and attempts to intercept.
3. Attackers may move along the boundaries or into open space.
4. The ball carrier scans both teammates.
5. The ball carrier draws the defender before releasing to the free player.
6. Attackers score one point for every three consecutive marks.
7. Rotate the defender after a turnover or set period.
8. Continue for multiple rounds.
9. Kicking distances must remain legal and appropriate for the group.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Maintain width.
Keep two clear options available.
Draw the defender without holding too long.
Kick to the free player’s advantage.
Move after disposal.
Avoid standing in the same lane.
Communicate early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether attackers stand in one line.
Whether the same player dominates possession.

commonErrors.error: Attackers stand too close together
commonErrors.correction: Spread to stretch the defender.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier releases before drawing pressure
commonErrors.correction: Hold briefly until the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: Player holds too long and becomes trapped
commonErrors.correction: Release as soon as the defender closes.

commonErrors.error: Targets remain stationary
commonErrors.correction: Adjust position to remain visible.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes too close to the defender
commonErrors.correction: Place the football away from pressure.

progressions: Require attackers to progress towards an end zone.
regressions: Use a coach as the defender.
matchApplication: Three-versus-one situations occur during: Defensive rebound. Overlap play. Switches. Loose-ball wins. Attacking transition.
relatedDrills: KK-066 – Possession Kick with End Zones

title: Possession Kick with End Zones
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession while progressing the football towards an end zone. Players learn to balance safe passing with forward movement and recognise when to retain, switch or attack.
setup:
• Create a rectangular playing area with an end zone at each end.
• Divide players into two teams.
• Recommended format:
• Five versus five.
• Six versus six.
• Optional neutral players along the outside.
• Each team attacks a nominated end zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The coach begins play with one team in possession.
2. Teams move the football using kicks.
3. A team scores by completing a marked kick to a teammate inside the attacking end zone.
4. Players may not remain permanently inside an end zone.
5. After a score, possession begins with the opposing team.
6. If the football is intercepted or leaves the area, possession changes.
7. Play for timed blocks.
8. Rotate the attacking direction.
9. Optional rules:
10. A minimum of three kicks before scoring.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Maintain width and depth.
Scan forward and sideways.
Avoid forcing forward kicks.
Use short possession to move defenders.
Recognise when the end zone becomes available.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Reposition after disposal.
coachingCues: “Attack the end zone at the right time.”

commonErrors.error: Players crowd near the attacking end zone
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width and depth across the full area.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier forces a forward kick
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession and move the defence first.

commonErrors.error: Receivers wait inside the end zone
commonErrors.correction: Time the lead into the scoring area.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal
commonErrors.correction: Reposition to support the next possession.

commonErrors.error: Team does not react after turnover
commonErrors.correction: Transition immediately into attack or defence.

progressions: Add a second football for separate groups.
matchApplication: This drill develops the balance between possession and territory during: Defensive exits. Controlled transitions. Late-game possession. Movement through zones. Attacking entries against an organised defence.

title: Four-versus-Two Kicking Grid
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession in a four-versus-two numerical advantage. Players learn to create width, provide multiple kicking options and move the football before the defenders can close the available lanes.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 12–18 using multiple groups
Maximum: 24
groundSize: Small to Medium Area Approximately 25 m × 20 m per group
setup:
• Create a rectangular grid.
• Place four attackers around the outside and inside edges of the grid.
• Position two defenders centrally.
• One attacker begins with the football.
• Recommended starting dimensions:
• Under 12–14: 25 m × 20 m.
• Under 16 and above: 22 m × 18 m.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attackers retain possession using kicks.
2. The defenders attempt to intercept, spoil or force an error.
3. The ball carrier may move a limited number of steps.
4. Attackers score one point for every four completed marks.
5. If the defenders win possession or force the football out, the player responsible for the turnover rotates into defence.
6. The longest-serving defender rotates out.
7. Continue for timed blocks.
8. Restart quickly after every turnover.
9. Optional rule:
10. At least one attacker must occupy the inside of the grid rather than all four remaining on the boundary.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Maintain width and depth.
Create at least two visible options.
Move before the football arrives.
Receive side-on.
Kick away from defensive pressure.
Avoid holding possession too long.
Reposition immediately after disposal.

commonErrors.error: Attackers stand in one line
commonErrors.correction: Create width, depth and an inside option.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier waits for pressure to arrive
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the next kick before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Players hide behind defenders
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally into a clear passing lane.

commonErrors.error: Kick is too high and slow
commonErrors.correction: Use a flatter, firmer short pass.

commonErrors.error: Same players remain uninvolved
commonErrors.correction: Rotate positions and demand movement from every attacker.

progressions: Remove the mark and continue play from any clean possession.
matchApplication: This drill develops possession under moderate pressure during: Defensive exits. Half-back control. Switching play. Numerical advantages. Late-game possession. Movement around a zone.
relatedDrills: KK-066 – Possession Kick with End Zones

title: Kicking Possession Transition Game
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession through kicking and transition immediately when possession changes. Players learn to spread quickly in attack, close space in defence and make effective decisions during turnover moments.
setup:
• Create a rectangular playing area.
• Divide players into two teams.
• Recommended formats:
• Five versus five with two neutral players.
• Six versus six.
• Seven versus seven in a larger area.
• Neutral players, if used, always play with the team in possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The coach begins play with one team.
2. The team in possession retains the football using kicks.
3. One point is awarded for every five consecutive marks.
4. If possession changes, the new attacking team spreads immediately.
5. The team that lost possession transitions into defence.
6. Play continues without stopping after interceptions or loose-ball wins.
7. Restart only when the football leaves the area or becomes trapped.
8. Play for timed blocks.
9. Optional scoring:
10. Two points for five consecutive kicks followed by a successful switch.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Spread immediately after winning possession.
Close space immediately after losing possession.
Scan before receiving.
Use short, accurate kicks.
Maintain width and depth.
Avoid kicking into central pressure.
Communicate during transition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Decision making immediately after possession changes.
Whether players switch mentally between attack and defence.

commonErrors.error: Players remain in attacking positions after losing possession
commonErrors.correction: Close the nearest space immediately.

commonErrors.error: Team wins possession but stays congested
commonErrors.correction: Spread quickly to create kicking lanes.

commonErrors.error: First kick after turnover is rushed
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the first safe option.

commonErrors.error: Players follow the football in a crowd
commonErrors.correction: Hold width and depth away from the contest.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase individually
commonErrors.correction: Coordinate pressure and protect central space.

matchApplication: Turnovers are among the most important moments in Australian Football. This drill develops the ability to: Attack before the opposition resets. Defend before the opposition spreads. Retain possession after winning the ball. Avoid immediate turnover chains. Use kicking skills under changing conditions.
relatedDrills: KK-066 – Possession Kick with End Zones

title: Zone-to-Zone Kicking Game
primarySkill: Progressing the Football Through Field Zones
objective: Develop the ability to progress possession through multiple field zones using controlled kicks. Players learn to create options ahead of the football, maintain support behind it and recognise when to retain or advance.
setup:
• Divide a rectangular playing area into three horizontal zones:
• Defensive zone.
• Midfield zone.
• Attacking zone.
• Divide players into two teams.
• Optional neutral players may operate in the midfield zone.
• Each team attacks a nominated end.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Play begins in one team’s defensive zone.
2. The team must progress the football through the midfield zone before entering the attacking zone.
3. Players may move between zones, but the coach may initially restrict numbers in each zone.
4. A point is scored when a player marks a kick inside the attacking end zone.
5. If possession changes, the new team attacks in the opposite direction.
6. Play continues through turnovers.
7. Restart after scores or when the football leaves the area.
8. Play for timed blocks.
9. Optional conditions:
10. At least one kick must be completed in each zone.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Create options ahead and behind the football.
Maintain width in every zone.
Avoid crowding the midfield.
Scan before receiving.
Recognise when the next zone is available.
Retain possession when forward lanes are closed.
Move after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players bypass the intended learning outcome.

commonErrors.error: All attackers move into the next zone
commonErrors.correction: Retain support behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Midfield zone becomes overcrowded
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width and stagger player depth.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier forces a kick forward
commonErrors.correction: Retain or switch until a lane opens.

commonErrors.error: Players remain in zones after turnover
commonErrors.correction: Transition immediately to the new direction.

commonErrors.error: Team kicks over zones without connection
commonErrors.correction: Require a possession in each zone.

regressions: Stop play after each successful zone entry.
matchApplication: This drill develops team kicking patterns across: Defensive exit. Midfield transition. Forward entry. Switches. Corridor movement. Controlled possession.
relatedDrills: KK-066 – Possession Kick with End Zones

title: Turnover Kick Challenge
objective: Develop the quality of the first kick after possession changes. Players learn to recognise whether to attack immediately, retain possession or move the football away from pressure following a turnover.
groundSize: Medium to Large Area Approximately 55 m × 40 m
setup:
• Create a rectangular playing area with one scoring target at each end.
• Divide players into two teams.
• The coach begins each repetition by creating a turnover through:
• A loose-ball feed.
• An intentionally intercepted pass.
• A contested possession.
• A coach’s call changing the attacking team.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. One team gains possession after the turnover.
2. The player winning the football must quickly assess:
3. Immediate forward option.
4. Safe lateral option.
5. Support behind the football.
6. The first kick is completed.
7. Play continues towards the attacking target.
8. The team scores by completing a marked kick in the end zone or kicking a goal.
9. If possession changes again, play continues in the opposite direction.
10. Reset after a score or the football leaves the area.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Secure possession first.
Lift the eyes immediately.
Recognise whether the opposition is organised.
Attack quickly when space is available.
Retain possession when the first forward option is unsafe.
Avoid blind kicks.
Use the first kick to establish team control.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players kick automatically without assessing.
Outcome of the first possession chain.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks immediately without looking
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and scan first.

commonErrors.error: Team wins the ball but remains congested
commonErrors.correction: Spread quickly to create options.

commonErrors.error: First kick goes back into pressure
commonErrors.correction: Use space away from the turnover area.

commonErrors.error: Player ignores an open attacking option
commonErrors.correction: Lift the eyes immediately after possession.

commonErrors.error: Team attacks recklessly against organised defence
commonErrors.correction: Retain and reset when forward lanes are closed.

regressions: Stop after the first kick for coaching.
matchApplication: The first kick after turnover can determine whether a team: Launches a fast attack. Retains possession. Re-enters congestion. Gives the football back. Creates a scoring opportunity.

title: Defensive-to-Attacking Transition Kick
primarySkill: Transition Kicking from Defence to Attack
objective: Develop the ability to move the football from a defensive possession into attack through a coordinated kicking chain. Players learn to spread quickly, identify the most dangerous available lane and support the football through multiple phases.
setup:
• Create:
• A defensive starting zone.
• A midfield transition zone.
• A forward scoring zone.
• Place one defensive player with the football or begin from an intercept feed.
• Position attacking teammates across half-back, wing, corridor and forward positions.
• Add passive defenders who recover as the ball moves.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The defensive player gains possession.
2. Attacking teammates spread immediately.
3. The defensive player selects the first outlet kick.
4. The receiving player scans and continues the transition through either:
5. The corridor.
6. A wide switch.
7. An overlap support option.
8. Defenders recover and attempt to close the available lanes.
9. The attacking team completes a forward entry and shot at goal.
10. If defenders win possession, they transition in the opposite direction.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Spread immediately after possession is won.
Maintain width and depth.
Scan before receiving.
Use the first safe kick to establish control.
Attack quickly if the opposition is unbalanced.
Switch if the direct side is closed.
Support behind and ahead of the football.

commonErrors.error: Players remain close to the defensive contest
commonErrors.correction: Spread immediately into transition positions.

commonErrors.error: First kick is forced into pressure
commonErrors.correction: Use a safe outlet to establish possession.

commonErrors.error: Team runs ahead without support behind
commonErrors.correction: Maintain players behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Ball movement becomes slow
commonErrors.correction: Prepare before receiving and use early options.

commonErrors.error: Final forward entry is rushed
commonErrors.correction: Maintain composure through the entire transition.

progressions: Require alternating corridor and wide transitions.
regressions: Stop after each kick for coaching.
matchApplication: This drill replicates full-field movement after: An intercept mark. A defensive ground-ball win. A turnover at half-back. A kick-in possession. A defensive stoppage clearance.

title: Intercept Mark Transition Kick
objective: Develop the ability to take an intercept mark, scan immediately and launch an effective transition kick before the opposition can recover defensively.
players:
Minimum: 9
Ideal: 12–21
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create:
• One attacking feeder outside a defensive zone.
• One intended attacking target.
• One intercept defender positioned between them.
• Three transition targets:
• Short outlet.
• Wide switch.
• Central attacking option.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder kicks towards the intended attacking target.
2. The intercept defender reads the kick and moves to mark.
3. As the intercept occurs, the three transition targets move into their lanes.
4. The intercept player scans immediately.
5. The intercept player selects and completes the best transition kick.
6. The receiver marks and continues the possession to a final target.
7. Players rotate through feeder, attacker, interceptor and transition roles.
8. Vary the location and height of the initial kick.
9. The intercept player may play on or use a controlled kick from the mark.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Read the ball flight.
Mark at the highest safe point.
Scan before landing where possible.
Secure the football.
Recognise opposition imbalance.
Use the first strong transition option.
Avoid automatically kicking down the line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Scanning before and after the mark.
Whether the player defaults to a predictable option.

commonErrors.error: Interceptor watches only the football
commonErrors.correction: Scan transition options as the ball arrives.

commonErrors.error: Player stops and holds possession unnecessarily
commonErrors.correction: Use the first strong option before defenders recover.

commonErrors.error: First kick goes back towards congestion
commonErrors.correction: Identify the open side.

commonErrors.error: Transition targets remain stationary
commonErrors.correction: Move immediately when the intercept is likely.

commonErrors.error: Interceptor rushes after a difficult mark
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and regain balance first.

progressions: Increase the difficulty of the intercept.
Allow a live attacker to pressure after the mark.
Continue into a full transition game.
regressions: Allow the interceptor to stop before disposal.
successIndicators: Move the football before defensive recovery.
matchApplication: Intercept marks create strong attacking opportunities because the opposition is often positioned for attack rather than defence. This drill develops the ability to convert an intercept into: A fast switch. A corridor transition. A safe short outlet. A forward attack. A repeat possession chain.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick

title: Intercept and Switch
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and execute a switch immediately after winning an intercept possession. Players learn to use the opposition’s movement towards one side to access space on the opposite side.
setup:
• Place:
• One feeder on a boundary side.
• One intended attacking target.
• One intercept player between them.
• One short release target centrally.
• One wide switch target on the opposite side.
• One forward outlet beyond the switch target.
• Add one or two recovering defenders.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder kicks towards the intended target.

title: Kick-In Short Option
objective: Develop the ability to execute a safe and accurate short kick from a kick-in situation. Players learn to coordinate the receiver’s lead with the kicker’s preparation and create a controlled first possession from defence.

Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using both sides

setup:

• One right.

• Place a second outlet target beyond each short receiver.
• Players form lines at kicker, short receiver and outlet positions.

1. The kicker retrieves or begins with the football.
2. The short receiver holds position until the kicker is ready.
3. The receiver leads towards open space.
4. The kicker delivers a short, firm pass.
5. The receiver marks and opens towards the next outlet.
6. The receiver kicks to the outlet target.
7. Players rotate through each role.
8. Alternate left and right options.
9. The receiver should not begin the lead so early that they become stationary.

Scan both short options.
Communicate with the receiver.
Wait for a decisive lead.
Use a firm, accurate kick.
Keep the football away from imaginary central pressure.
Position the receiver side-on.
Prepare the next disposal before the mark.

Whether the same option is used repeatedly.

title: Elite Decision-Making Under Pressure
primarySkill: Selecting and Executing the Best Kicking Option Under Pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to scan, assess risk and execute the highest-value kicking option while under immediate physical and time pressure.
setup:
• Divide players into two teams.
• Mark three vertical kicking channels:
• Boundary channel.
• Central channel.
• Opposite-side channel.

• Assign different point values to each target based on difficulty and tactical value.
• Begin each repetition with a contested possession or coach-fed football.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. A player wins or receives possession under defensive pressure.
2. The player has a limited period to scan and dispose of the football.
3. Teammates create short, medium and long options.
4. The player selects the most appropriate kick based on:
5. Defensive positioning.
6. Available space.
7. Teammate movement.
8. Turnover risk.
9. Play continues for three to five disposals.
10. A turnover immediately changes the direction of play.

7. Play resets after each outcome.
