Maintain an inside release option.
Use depth behind the football.
Avoid leading every player into the same space.
Recognise when to take territory.
Prepare for a boundary stoppage if possession cannot be retained.
Transition immediately if the football is turned over.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Placement of kicks relative to the boundary.

commonErrors.error: Kick drifts too close to the boundary
commonErrors.correction: Aim to the receiver’s inside shoulder.

commonErrors.error: All players lead in a straight line
commonErrors.correction: Create depth and different angles.

commonErrors.error: No inside release option
commonErrors.correction: Hold one player inside the channel.

commonErrors.error: Player forces a short kick under pressure
commonErrors.correction: Take territory when possession is unlikely.

commonErrors.error: Team does not prepare for turnover
commonErrors.correction: Maintain defensive balance behind the ball.

progressions: Add a central bonus gate that may open unexpectedly.
Require a mark before entering the target zone.
successIndicators: Place kicks to the safe side.
matchApplication: Replicates boundary-side exits when the opposition has closed the corridor.

title: Corridor Re-Entry Kick
primarySkill: Re-Entering the Corridor After Boundary Possession
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and execute the correct moment to move the football from the boundary back into the corridor.
setup:
• Mark a boundary channel and a central corridor.
• Begin possession in the boundary channel.
• Position central attackers and defenders in the corridor.
• Create two central entry gates.
• The coach may open or close gates using coloured signals.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacking team moves the football along the boundary.
2. Central players continually reposition to create an entry lane.
3. The ball carrier scans for the corridor option.
4. When the corridor becomes available, the player executes the re-entry kick.
5. The team accelerates forward following the central connection.
6. If the corridor remains closed, the team retains possession or continues along the boundary.
7. A turnover immediately reverses the direction of play.
coachingPoints: Avoid entering the corridor without forward support.
Wait until the central receiver has separation.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Move quickly after the central kick.
Maintain width until the corridor opportunity appears.
Recognise whether the defence is shifting or stationary.
Avoid telegraphing the kick too early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Speed of transition after the kick.

commonErrors.error: Corridor kick is forced into congestion
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until separation appears.

commonErrors.error: Receiver is stationary
commonErrors.correction: Lead through the available window.

commonErrors.error: No forward support after central entry
commonErrors.correction: Push runners ahead before the kick.

commonErrors.error: Kicker telegraphs the option
commonErrors.correction: Continue scanning and disguise the disposal.

commonErrors.error: Team collapses centrally too early
commonErrors.correction: Maintain boundary width until the moment of entry.

progressions: Reduce the width of the corridor.
Require a forward-50 entry after corridor connection.
Allow defenders to change structure during play.
successIndicators: Recognise the correct corridor entry moment.
Maintain structure before and after the kick.
matchApplication: Replicates switching from controlled boundary play into aggressive corridor transition.

title: Defensive Switch Intercept Risk
primarySkill: Executing Defensive Switches Without Exposing Intercept Opportunities
objective: Develop players’ understanding of when a defensive switch is available and how to execute it without creating a dangerous central turnover.
setup:
• Position the attacking team across defensive 50.
• Place pressing forwards between the ball and the opposite side.
• Create short, medium and long switch options.
• Mark a central turnover zone where defensive interceptions receive bonus points.
• Begin with a mark near one boundary.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier assesses whether the switch is available.
2. Teammates move to create safe angles and depth.
3. The team may:
4. Complete the switch.
5. Retain possession.
6. Exit down the original side.
7. Defenders attempt to anticipate and intercept the switch.
8. The attacking team scores by reaching the opposite wing under control.
9. The defending team receives extra points for intercepting centrally.
10. Reset after the outcome.
coachingPoints: Ensure the switch receiver has separation.
Avoid slow, floating kicks.
Use sufficient depth behind the football.
Check for hidden defenders.
Communicate whether the switch is safe.
Keep an exit option on the original side.
Understand that not every switch should be completed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players retain the original-side option.

commonErrors.error: Switch kick hangs in the air
commonErrors.correction: Use a lower, faster trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Receiver stands level with the ball
commonErrors.correction: Create greater depth behind possession.

commonErrors.error: Kicker does not scan central defenders
commonErrors.correction: Check the entire lane before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Team commits fully to the switch
commonErrors.correction: Keep an option on the original side.

commonErrors.error: Switch is forced because it was planned
commonErrors.correction: Read the defence and cancel when necessary.

successIndicators: Identify whether the switch is genuinely available.
matchApplication: Replicates defensive switches against organised forward-half pressure.
relatedDrills: KK-128 – Switch Completion to Forward Entry

title: Switch Completion to Forward Entry
primarySkill: Converting a Defensive Switch into an Attacking Forward Entry
objective: Develop the team’s ability to complete a defensive switch, accelerate through the open side and finish with a high-quality forward-50 entry.
setup:
• Position players in defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
• Begin with possession near one defensive boundary.
• Set defenders to protect the initial side.
• Leave the opposite wing partially open.
• Position forwards to begin moving only after the switch is initiated.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The defending team initiates a switch across defensive 50.
2. Once the opposite-side receiver marks the football, the team accelerates.
3. Wing and midfield players provide forward-running options.
4. The ball must move through at least one midfield connection.
5. The team completes the sequence with an inside-50 kick.
6. Forwards attempt to mark or create a scoring opportunity.
7. A turnover results in immediate defensive transition.
8. Reset from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: Complete the switch with speed and accuracy.
Accelerate once the open side is accessed.
Run ahead of the football.
Maintain central and boundary options.
Avoid slowing the play after gaining advantage.
Deliver inside 50 to space rather than directly at defenders.
Maintain defensive balance behind the ball.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the team attacks immediately after shifting the defence.

commonErrors.error: Play remains slow after the switch
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately once the open side is gained.

commonErrors.error: Runners wait for the next kick
commonErrors.correction: Begin forward movement as the switch travels.

commonErrors.error: Team uses only the boundary
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a central connection option.

commonErrors.error: Final entry is rushed
commonErrors.correction: Assess forward separation before kicking.

commonErrors.error: Defenders push too far forward
commonErrors.correction: Retain coverage behind the football.

progressions: Set a maximum time to enter forward 50.
Require a goal to complete the repetition.
Allow defenders to block the preferred switch side.
regressions: Reduce the number of midfield connections.
matchApplication: Replicates full-ground transition after successfully shifting an opposition defensive press.

title: Turnover Punishment Kick Chain
primarySkill: Attacking Immediately After an Opposition Turnover
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and exploit opposition disorganisation immediately after winning possession from a turnover.
setup:
• Create two teams in realistic field positions.
• The coach begins with controlled possession by one team.
• At a random moment, the coach creates a turnover through:
• A misplaced kick.
• A loose football.
• An intercept opportunity.
• A whistle and possession reversal.
• Place scoring targets at the attacking end.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. One team begins in possession.
2. The coach creates an unexpected turnover.
3. The new attacking team must immediately spread and attack.
4. The first player in possession assesses:
5. Corridor.
6. Wide outlet.
7. Forward isolation.
8. Short retention option.
9. The team attempts to complete a scoring chain before the opposition resets.
10. If the opposition regains possession, direction reverses again.
coachingPoints: Scan forward immediately after winning possession.
Recognise when the opposition is out of shape.
Move the football before the defence recovers.
Run aggressively into open space.
Avoid attacking blindly when no advantage exists.
Lower the eyes before entering forward 50.
Communicate the turnover immediately.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: First kicking decision after the turnover.
Defensive reaction from the team that lost possession.
Whether players recognise when to slow down.

commonErrors.error: Players hesitate after the turnover
commonErrors.correction: Scan forward and attack immediately when advantage exists.

commonErrors.error: First kick is rushed blindly
commonErrors.correction: Assess numbers before disposing.

commonErrors.error: Teammates remain in defensive positions
commonErrors.correction: Spread and run forward immediately.

commonErrors.error: Ball is kicked long to an outnumbered contest
commonErrors.correction: Use a shorter connection to preserve the advantage.

commonErrors.error: Team continues attacking after the defence resets
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession and rebuild shape.

progressions: Require the first disposal to be a kick.
Begin from different areas of the ground.
Allow repeated turnovers within the same play.
regressions: Announce the turnover before it occurs.
successIndicators: Recognise when the transition advantage has ended.
matchApplication: Replicates scoring chains created from intercept marks, pressure turnovers and loose-ball recoveries.
relatedDrills: KK-128 – Switch Completion to Forward Entry

title: Turnover Recovery Kick
primarySkill: Regaining Controlled Possession After Losing the Football
objective: Develop the team’s ability to respond after a kicking turnover, regain possession and execute a controlled recovery kick rather than immediately turning the football over again.
setup:
• Divide players into two teams.
• Mark two recovery target gates on opposite sides of the area.
• Begin with one team moving the football by foot.
• The coach calls or creates a turnover.
• The team that lost possession must apply immediate pressure and attempt to regain the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacking team begins a kicking chain.
2. A turnover occurs naturally or is created by the coach.
3. The team that lost possession applies immediate pressure.
4. If possession is regained, the player must execute a controlled recovery kick through one of the target gates.
5. The recovery kick cannot be a blind clearance unless no possession option exists.
6. The opposition attempts to force a second turnover.
7. Teams receive points for:
8. Regaining possession.
9. Completing the recovery kick.
10. Preventing a score.
coachingPoints: React immediately after losing possession.
Close the ball carrier’s options.
Protect dangerous central space.
Stay composed when possession is regained.
Look for a safe outlet before clearing.
Use the boundary if the team remains under pressure.
Rebuild offensive shape after the recovery kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Pressure applied to the new ball carrier.
Selection and execution of the recovery kick.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after losing possession
commonErrors.correction: Demand an immediate defensive reaction.

commonErrors.error: Team chases the football and leaves the corridor open
commonErrors.correction: Protect central space while applying pressure.

commonErrors.error: First possession after recovery is rushed
commonErrors.correction: Secure the football and identify a safe outlet.

commonErrors.error: Recovery kick is directed back into congestion
commonErrors.correction: Use width or the boundary-side option.

commonErrors.error: Players relax after completing the kick
commonErrors.correction: Rebuild attacking and defensive structure immediately.

progressions: Add a time limit for the recovery kick.
Require the recovery chain to continue into attack.
regressions: Allow additional time after the regain.
Increase the size of target gates.
matchApplication: Replicates the critical moments following a kicking error when teams must defend, regain control and reconnect with a safe disposal.

title: Defensive Scramble Release Kick
primarySkill: Executing a Controlled Release Kick from Defensive Scramble
objective: Develop players’ ability to regain possession in a disorganised defensive situation and execute a controlled release kick rather than a blind clearance into further pressure.
setup:
• Position attackers and defenders inside defensive 50.
• Create two wide release gates and one central release gate outside the area.
• The coach begins each repetition with an unpredictable high ball, ground ball or deflection.
• Defenders begin slightly out of position to create a realistic scramble.
• Attackers attempt to win possession and score.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The coach introduces an unpredictable football into defensive 50.
2. Defenders compete to spoil, gather or intercept.
3. Once possession is secured, the defending team must identify a release option.
4. The first kick should connect with a teammate or travel safely through a release gate.
5. Attackers apply immediate pressure and attempt to force a turnover.
6. The defending team scores for exiting under control.
7. Attackers score by winning possession and kicking a goal.
8. Reset with players in different starting positions.
coachingPoints: Secure possession before attempting the release.
Scan outside the contest before gathering.
Protect the corridor during the scramble.
Use the boundary when central options are unsafe.
Avoid kicking directly back into congestion.
Communicate available release options early.
Rebuild team structure after the exit.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Direction and placement of the release kick.
Reactions if the first release option is denied.

commonErrors.error: Blind kick from congestion
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and scan for an outlet.

commonErrors.error: Release kick travels centrally under pressure
commonErrors.correction: Use the boundary-side option when the corridor is unsafe.

commonErrors.error: Outside players stand too close to the contest
commonErrors.correction: Create width and depth outside the pressure area.

commonErrors.error: Defender attempts too much with the first disposal
commonErrors.correction: Complete the safe release before accelerating play.

commonErrors.error: Team stops after exiting
commonErrors.correction: Reposition immediately to support the next possession.

progressions: Reduce the size of the defensive area.
Require the exit to continue into a forward entry.
successIndicators: Win or secure the defensive football.
Re-establish team structure after the scramble.
matchApplication: Replicates defensive ground-ball contests, spoils and loose-ball situations where a composed exit kick can prevent repeat opposition entries.

title: Repeat Entry Defensive Exit
primarySkill: Exiting Defensive 50 After Repeated Opposition Entries
objective: Develop the ability to withstand repeated forward entries, regain control and execute a composed defensive exit while players are fatigued and structurally disrupted.
setup:
• Position one team inside defensive 50.
• Place attacking players across the forward half.
• Keep several footballs with coaches positioned outside the area.
• Mark an exit line approximately 20 metres beyond defensive 50.
• Defenders must successfully exit the football to end the repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The coach delivers the first football into attacking 50.
2. Attackers attempt to score.
3. If defenders spoil, intercept or win possession but fail to exit, the coach introduces another football.
4. The sequence continues until:
5. The defending team completes a controlled exit beyond the exit line.
6. The attacking team scores a goal.
7. A predetermined number of entries is completed.
8. Defenders must maintain communication and structure despite fatigue.
9. Teams rotate after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Defend the most dangerous space first.
Stay connected after every contest.
Spread immediately when possession is won.
Avoid rushing the first exit kick.
Use short possession to create a safer long exit.
Recognise when territory is more valuable than retention.
Maintain concentration through repeated phases.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Speed of spread after possession is won.
Quality of the first exit decision.
Whether players repeat the same unsuccessful exit.
Work rate after a failed clearance.

commonErrors.error: Defenders remain compressed after winning possession
commonErrors.correction: Spread immediately to create outlets.

commonErrors.error: First kick is rushed to an outnumbered contest
commonErrors.correction: Use a short connection or safer side.

commonErrors.error: Players lose opponents after repeated entries
commonErrors.correction: Reorganise roles after every phase.

commonErrors.error: Team repeatedly exits through the same area
commonErrors.correction: Scan both sides and vary the release.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes poor communication
commonErrors.correction: Demand clear calls throughout the sequence.

progressions: Increase the number of repeat entries.
Require two completed kicks before the exit counts.
regressions: Allow defenders a free kick after an intercept mark.
Limit the number of repeat entries.
Use controlled rather than full pressure.
successIndicators: Maintain defensive structure through repeated phases.
matchApplication: Replicates sustained opposition pressure when a team must absorb repeated inside-50 entries before successfully rebounding.

title: Long Down-the-Line Contest Kick
primarySkill: Executing a Long Kick to a Boundary-Side Contest
objective: Develop the ability to execute a long down-the-line kick that gives teammates the best chance to mark, force a stoppage or bring the football safely to ground.
setup:
• Mark a boundary channel.
• Position a kicker approximately 45–60 metres from a target contest.
• Place one target player and one defender at the contest.
• Position two ground-level support players around the drop zone.
• Mark a safe landing zone between the target and the boundary.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker receives the football under controlled pressure.
2. The target player leads or holds position down the line.
3. The kicker delivers a long kick into the safe landing zone.
4. The target attempts to mark or bring the football to ground safely.
5. Ground-level players compete for the crumb.
6. The attacking team scores for:
7. A mark.
8. A boundary stoppage.
9. Controlled possession from the contest.
10. The defending team scores for an uncontested intercept or clean rebound.
coachingPoints: Kick to the boundary side of the target.
Give the target sufficient height and time when required.
Avoid placing the football inside where defenders can counterattack.
Match trajectory to the target’s positioning.
Ensure ground-level support arrives at the drop zone.
Maintain defensive coverage behind the kick.
Understand when a contest kick is tactically appropriate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Kick placement relative to the target.
Outcome when the mark is not taken.

commonErrors.error: Kick lands inside the target
commonErrors.correction: Direct the football towards the boundary-side shoulder.

commonErrors.error: Kick travels too flat for the distance
commonErrors.correction: Add appropriate height to allow the target to compete.

commonErrors.error: Target waits directly under the football
commonErrors.correction: Establish front position and protect the drop zone.

commonErrors.error: No support arrives at ground level
commonErrors.correction: Send players to the front and defensive side of the contest.

commonErrors.error: Players assume the long kick must be marked
commonErrors.correction: Prepare for a spill or boundary stoppage.

progressions: Introduce live pressure on the kicker.
Allow the contest to continue into transition.
regressions: Allow the kicker additional preparation time.
successIndicators: Place the football on the safe side.
Give the target a genuine opportunity to compete.
Achieve a mark, stoppage or controlled ground-ball win.
matchApplication: Replicates long boundary exits and territory kicks when short possession or corridor options are unavailable.

title: Contest Kick Ground-Level Setup
primarySkill: Supporting a Long Contest Kick at Ground Level
objective: Develop coordinated positioning around a long kicking contest so the team is prepared to win the spill, force a stoppage or defend an opposition possession.
setup:
• Create a long-kick starting point and a marked contest zone.
• Position one aerial target and one direct opponent inside the zone.
• Place attacking support players at:
• Front of the contest.
• Boundary side.
• Defensive side.
• Place matching defenders around the area.
• Begin each repetition with a long kick into the contest.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker delivers to the aerial contest.
2. The target attempts to mark or direct the football to a designated area.
3. Ground-level players hold their roles until the ball’s flight is clear.
4. Players compete for the spill.
5. The team winning possession must complete a kick through a target gate.
6. If the football leaves the area, reset and rotate positions.
coachingPoints: Avoid all players moving directly underneath the football.
Cover front, boundary and defensive-side positions.
Read the likely direction of the spoil.
Communicate role ownership.
Maintain balance between attack and defence.
Use the first possession cleanly after the contest.
React immediately if the opposition wins the ball.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Defensive reaction when possession is lost.

commonErrors.error: Too many players compete in the air
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one aerial player and keep others at ground level.

commonErrors.error: Ground-level players crowd the drop zone
commonErrors.correction: Maintain separate front, side and defensive positions.

commonErrors.error: Players move before reading the flight
commonErrors.correction: Hold structure until the likely landing point is clear.

commonErrors.error: First possession is rushed
commonErrors.correction: Secure the football and identify the release target.

commonErrors.error: No defensive cover behind the contest
commonErrors.correction: Keep one player goal-side or behind the drop zone.

progressions: Add more players around the contest.
Continue play into a scoring zone.
regressions: Allow the coach to position players before each contest.
successIndicators: Avoid overcommitting to the aerial contest.
Complete a controlled disposal after possession.
matchApplication: Replicates team structure around long boundary kicks, stoppage exits and contested forward entries.

title: Outnumbered Contest Kick
primarySkill: Managing a Necessary Kick to an Outnumbered Contest
objective: Develop players’ ability to minimise turnover damage when a kick to an outnumbered contest is unavoidable.
setup:
• Position one attacking target against two defenders.
• Place the contest near a boundary.
• Position one or two attacking ground-level support players outside the contest.
• The kicker begins under pressure with no uncontested short option.
• Mark a safe territory zone beyond the contest.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker scans for alternatives before deciding to kick long.
2. When the contest kick is required, the kicker places the football towards the boundary side.
3. The attacking target competes to:
4. Mark.
5. Force the football out.
6. Bring it to a predictable ground-level area.
7. Support players attempt to win the spill or force a stoppage.
8. Defenders attempt to intercept and rebound.
9. Points are awarded based on the outcome:
10. Mark by the target.
coachingPoints: Confirm that no safer option exists.
Kick away from the most dangerous opposition space.
Use the boundary as protection.
Give the target sufficient time to compete.
Avoid kicking short of the contest.
Position support players for the likely spill.
Prepare defensively if the opposition intercepts.

commonErrors.error: Kicker ignores a safer short option
commonErrors.correction: Scan fully before committing to the contest kick.

commonErrors.error: Kick lands centrally
commonErrors.correction: Use the boundary-side landing zone.

commonErrors.error: Ball drops short of the target
commonErrors.correction: Kick beyond or directly to the target’s advantage.

commonErrors.error: Target attempts an unrealistic mark from behind
commonErrors.correction: Focus on bringing the football safely to ground.

commonErrors.error: Support players arrive late
commonErrors.correction: Move as soon as the kick decision becomes clear.

progressions: Introduce a second attacking support player.
Allow full live transition after the contest.
regressions: Use one defender instead of two.
Allow the target to begin in front position.
Use passive pressure on the kicker.
successIndicators: Recognise when the contest kick is necessary.
Place the football in a low-risk area.
Force stoppages or win ground-level possession.
Maintain defensive balance behind the kick.
matchApplication: Replicates situations where pressure and field position require a territory kick despite an opposition numerical advantage.

title: Numerical Advantage Recognition Kick
primarySkill: Identifying and Kicking to a Numerical Advantage
objective: Develop players’ ability to quickly recognise numerical advantages around the ground and deliver the football to the area where their team has superior numbers.
setup:
• Mark three target zones across the ground.
• Position different numbers of attackers and defenders in each zone.
• Change the numerical balance before every repetition.
• Place a ball carrier approximately 30–45 metres from the zones.
• Add one pressure defender near the kicker.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker scans all three zones.
2. Players inside the zones move to create separation.
3. The kicker identifies where the attacking team has:
4. A clear numerical advantage.
5. The strongest positional advantage.
6. The safest next-possession opportunity.
7. The kicker delivers to the selected zone.
8. Players compete and attempt to complete a follow-up kick.
9. The coach changes numbers and positioning before the next repetition.
10. Rotate kickers and zone players.
coachingPoints: Count numbers before receiving.
Distinguish between numerical and positional advantage.
Avoid kicking to a crowded zone simply because it is closer.
Weight the kick to allow teammates to use their numbers.
Communicate the advantage clearly.
Reassess if defenders move during preparation.
Follow the kick to support the next possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Ability to adjust when the advantage changes.

commonErrors.error: Kicker focuses only on the nearest zone
commonErrors.correction: Scan all available areas before deciding.

commonErrors.error: Player confuses numbers with genuine advantage
commonErrors.correction: Assess positioning and defender access as well as numbers.

commonErrors.error: Kick is too slow and allows defenders to recover
commonErrors.correction: Deliver quickly once the advantage is identified.

commonErrors.error: Kick lands directly on top of the group
commonErrors.correction: Place the football into space for teammates to use their numbers.

commonErrors.error: Kicker does not support after disposal
commonErrors.correction: Follow the kick and connect to the next phase.

progressions: Conceal player numbers until the kicker turns to receive.
regressions: Pause before each repetition for guided scanning.
matchApplication: Replicates the scanning and tactical awareness required to exploit spare players during transition, switches and forward entries.

title: Spare Player Elimination Kick
primarySkill: Kicking Around or Through an Opposition Spare Player
objective: Develop the ability to identify an opposition spare player and use intelligent kicking, movement and field position to reduce that player’s influence.
equipment: Coloured vest for the spare defender
setup:
• Position one team in possession across half-back and midfield.
• Place forwards in attacking positions.
• Nominate one defender as the spare player.
• The spare may position behind the ball or in front of the key forward.
• Mark wide, central and short-entry zones.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacking team begins with possession outside forward 50.
2. Players identify the spare defender’s location.
3. The team attempts to move the spare through:
4. Switching play.
5. Short possession.
6. Changing angles.
7. Using a player behind the ball.
8. Once the spare is displaced, the team enters forward 50.
9. The spare defender attempts to intercept and launch a rebound.
10. The attacking team scores for creating a mark or controlled possession inside 50.
coachingPoints: Identify the spare before entering forward 50.
Avoid repeatedly kicking directly to the spare.
Use possession to move the defender laterally.
Create a short option in front of the defensive block.
Change the entry angle.
Use forwards to occupy and manipulate defenders.
Maintain defensive balance in case of turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Quality of switches and short connections.
Forward movement designed to occupy defenders.

commonErrors.error: Ball is repeatedly kicked to the spare
commonErrors.correction: Scan the defensive setup and change the entry angle.

commonErrors.error: Team attacks before moving the defence
commonErrors.correction: Use possession to shift the spare first.

commonErrors.error: Forwards remain stationary
commonErrors.correction: Create movement to occupy and displace defenders.

commonErrors.error: Players switch without gaining an advantage
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate once the spare is moved.

commonErrors.error: Team pushes every player forward
commonErrors.correction: Retain defensive coverage behind the football.

progressions: Allow the spare to change positions during play.
Require a score to complete the repetition.
regressions: Restrict the spare to one zone.
Pause play to identify the spare.
matchApplication: Replicates attacking against an opposition loose defender positioned behind the ball or in front of a key forward.
relatedDrills: KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure

title: Defensive Zone Penetration Kick
objective: Develop the ability to identify and execute kicks that penetrate an organised defensive zone without exposing the team to high-risk turnovers.
setup:
• Divide the ground into defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
• Position the defending team in an organised zone structure.
• The attacking team begins with controlled possession in the defensive half.
• Mark bonus gates between defenders in the midfield and forward lines.
• The attacking team must penetrate the zone primarily through kicking.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacking team circulates possession to move the zone.
2. Players ahead of the football adjust their positioning to create passing lanes.
3. The ball carrier identifies whether to:
4. Kick through the zone.
5. Kick around the zone.
6. Retain possession.
7. Take territory to a contest.
8. Bonus points are awarded for penetrating through a gate and retaining possession.
9. The defending team attempts to intercept and counterattack.
10. Play continues until a score, turnover or successful exit.
coachingPoints: Move the zone before attempting penetration.
Scan through the defensive line rather than only around it.
Use sharp-angle kicks where safe.
Position receivers between defensive lines.
Avoid slow, floating passes through central space.
Accelerate after breaking one line.
Maintain options behind the ball.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Movement of players between defensive lines.
Timing and trajectory of penetrating kicks.
Ability to recognise when penetration is unsafe.

commonErrors.error: Penetrating kick is attempted before the zone moves
commonErrors.correction: Use possession to shift defenders first.

commonErrors.error: Receiver stands directly behind a defender
commonErrors.correction: Reposition between lines and outside the defender’s vision.

commonErrors.error: Kick floats through central space
commonErrors.correction: Use a faster, flatter trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Team slows after breaking the first line
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate while the zone is disorganised.

commonErrors.error: Players behind the ball stop supporting
commonErrors.correction: Maintain reset and defensive-cover options.

regressions: Walk through the defensive structure before live play.
successIndicators: Move the defensive zone before attacking it.
matchApplication: Replicates controlled ball movement against teams defending with organised zones, presses or layered structures.

title: Defensive Line-Breaking Kick
primarySkill: Breaking a Defensive Line with an Aggressive Kick
objective: Develop players’ ability to identify and execute a high-value kick that breaks an opposition defensive line and creates immediate attacking momentum.
setup:
• Mark three horizontal defensive lines across the area.
• Position defenders along each line.
• Place attacking receivers in spaces between and beyond the lines.
• Begin with possession behind the first defensive line.
• Mark bonus zones beyond each line.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacking team begins with controlled possession.
2. Players move to create a passing lane through or over a defensive line.
3. The ball carrier assesses whether a line-breaking kick is available.
4. A successful kick must:
5. Bypass at least one defensive line.
6. Connect with a teammate.
7. Allow the team to retain attacking momentum.
8. The receiver plays on or quickly moves the football forward.
9. The defending team attempts to intercept and counterattack.
10. Play continues until the final target zone is reached or possession changes.
coachingPoints: Scan beyond the nearest option.
Ensure the receiver has separation.
Use the correct trajectory for the available lane.
Avoid forcing line-breaking kicks into organised numbers.
Run forward immediately after the kick.
Provide support on both sides of the receiver.
Recognise when a safer possession kick is required.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Forward support after the line break.
Team reaction when the kick is unavailable.

commonErrors.error: Player automatically selects the nearest option
commonErrors.correction: Scan beyond the first defensive line.

commonErrors.error: Kick is forced without receiver separation
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until a clear lane appears.

commonErrors.error: Receiver remains stationary
commonErrors.correction: Lead into space between or beyond the lines.

commonErrors.error: Team admires the successful kick
commonErrors.correction: Run immediately to support the next possession.

commonErrors.error: Kicker attempts excessive difficulty
commonErrors.correction: Match risk to field position and team structure.

progressions: Add pressure to the ball carrier.
Reduce the width of passing lanes.
Continue into a full-ground scoring sequence.
successIndicators: Execute kicks with appropriate speed and accuracy.
matchApplication: Replicates aggressive kicks that bypass opposition defensive layers and launch rapid attacking transition.

title: Advanced Kicking Scenario Assessment
primarySkill: Applying Advanced Kicking Decisions Across Match Scenarios
objective: Assess players’ ability to apply advanced kicking skills across a range of realistic match scenarios involving defensive exits, numerical advantages, contested kicking, zone penetration and turnover management.
setup:
• Create ten advanced kicking scenarios across the ground:
• Defensive scramble release.
• Repeat-entry exit.
• Long boundary contest kick.
• Ground-level contest setup.
• Outnumbered contest management.
• Numerical advantage recognition.
• Opposition spare-player manipulation.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The coach begins each scenario from a realistic match position.
2. Players receive limited information before play begins.
3. The team must identify the tactical problem and execute an appropriate kicking solution.
4. Each scenario continues until:
5. The tactical objective is achieved.
6. A score occurs.
7. Possession changes.
8. The allotted time expires.
9. Coaches assess:
10. Decision quality.
coachingPoints: Scan before gaining possession.
Understand field position and turnover consequences.
Match the kick type to the tactical problem.
Communicate the intended option early.
Maintain support ahead of and behind the football.
Adjust immediately when the preferred option closes.
Evaluate outcomes without becoming outcome-focused.
Preserve technical execution under fatigue.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Understanding of numerical and positional advantage.

commonErrors.error: Players predetermine the disposal
commonErrors.correction: Scan and respond to the actual defensive picture.

commonErrors.error: Technical execution deteriorates under fatigue
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish balance, ball control and follow-through.

commonErrors.error: Players choose excessive risk in defensive areas
commonErrors.correction: Match risk to field position and team coverage.

commonErrors.error: Team fails to support the selected option
commonErrors.correction: Move before the kick and connect around the receiver.

commonErrors.error: Players repeat unsuccessful solutions
commonErrors.correction: Identify how the opposition has adjusted and change the approach.

commonErrors.error: Communication declines late in the assessment
commonErrors.correction: Maintain clear role and option calls throughout.

progressions: Allow opposition coaches to adjust defensive structures.
Add fatigue efforts before each scenario.
Run all scenarios within one continuous match simulation.
successIndicators: Maintain team structure around the football.
Apply advanced kicking principles across multiple field positions.
matchApplication: Provides a comprehensive assessment of advanced kicking decisions required during defensive exits, contested ball movement, transition, forward entry and late-game situations.

title: Elite Full-Ground Kicking Simulation
primarySkill: Executing Team Kicking Strategy Across the Full Ground
objective: Develop the team’s ability to execute its complete kicking system from defensive possession through midfield and into attack against realistic opposition pressure.
setup:
• Divide players into two balanced teams.
• Establish realistic positional structures.
• Mark defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
• Begin repetitions from:
• Kick-ins.
• Intercept marks.
• Centre clearances.
• Boundary stoppages.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Play begins from a nominated match situation.
2. The team in possession must move the football primarily by foot.
3. Players may use:
4. Short possession.
5. Defensive switches.
6. Boundary exits.
7. Corridor attacks.
8. Long contest kicks.
9. The team attempts to create a controlled inside-50 entry and scoring opportunity.
10. Turnovers result in immediate live transition.
coachingPoints: Scan before receiving.
Maintain width and depth.
Support ahead of and behind the football.
Recognise when to accelerate or retain possession.
Match risk to field position.
Lower the eyes before entering forward 50.
Maintain defensive balance while attacking.
Transition immediately after turnovers.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd the ball side
commonErrors.correction: Maintain opposite-side width.

commonErrors.error: Team attacks at one speed
commonErrors.correction: Change tempo according to the defensive structure.

commonErrors.error: Long kicks are directed to outnumbered contests
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession or change the entry angle.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal
commonErrors.correction: Continue supporting the possession chain.

commonErrors.error: Defensive structure disappears during attack
commonErrors.correction: Hold coverage behind the football.

progressions: Give the opposition an extra defender.
Require specific exit or entry patterns.
matchApplication: Replicates complete AFL match ball movement and kicking decision making across all areas of the ground.

title: Opposition Press Adaptation
primarySkill: Adapting Kicking Strategy to Different Defensive Presses
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise different opposition defensive presses and adjust their kicking strategy without requiring direct instruction from the coach.
setup:
• Prepare several defensive structures:
• Full-ground press.
• Half-ground press.
• Boundary trap.
• Corridor block.
• Man-on-man defence.
• Loose defender behind the ball.
• The defending team changes its structure before or during each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacking team begins with possession in defence.
2. The opposition establishes one of the nominated presses.
3. The attacking team must identify the structure without coach assistance.
4. Players select an appropriate exit strategy.
5. Play continues until the attacking team:
6. Reaches the wing.
7. Exits the defensive half.
8. Creates a forward entry.
9. A turnover allows the defending team to attack.
10. The defensive structure changes for the next repetition.
coachingPoints: Identify where the opposition has placed extra numbers.
Recognise which areas have been deliberately left open.
Avoid using the same exit pattern repeatedly.
Move defenders before attempting penetration.
Use short kicks to open long options.
Change tempo when the opposition adjusts.
Communicate the identified defensive structure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Execution after the press is beaten.
Reaction when the first option closes.

commonErrors.error: Team uses a predetermined exit
commonErrors.correction: Read the opposition structure first.

commonErrors.error: Players attack the most heavily defended area
commonErrors.correction: Identify where the opposition has conceded space.

commonErrors.error: Switch is completed too slowly
commonErrors.correction: Move the football before defenders recover.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to communicate the press
commonErrors.correction: Nominate leaders to identify the structure aloud.

commonErrors.error: Team relaxes after beating the first line
commonErrors.correction: Continue attacking while the opposition is disorganised.

Prevent coaches from announcing the press.
Let the defending team design its own press.
regressions: Walk through each press before live play.
successIndicators: Adjust when the defensive structure changes.
matchApplication: Replicates preparing for and responding to different opposition defensive systems.

title: Weather-Condition Kicking
primarySkill: Adapting Kicking Technique to Weather Conditions
objective: Develop players’ ability to adjust kicking technique, kick selection and team strategy according to wind, rain and difficult ground conditions.
equipment: Water bottles or damp footballs where appropriate
setup:
• Create stations or scenarios representing:
• Kicking with the wind.
• Kicking into the wind.
• Crosswind kicking.
• Wet-football possession.
• Slippery ground-ball recovery.
• Long territory kicking.
• Short controlled possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Players rotate through each weather-based scenario.
2. At every station, the kicker must adjust:
3. Ball drop.
4. Kick trajectory.
5. Power.
6. Target position.
7. Team-based phases require players to decide whether to:
8. Retain possession.
9. Take territory.
10. Use the boundary.
coachingPoints: Lower kick trajectory into the wind.
Avoid excessive ball height in strong crosswinds.
Keep the ball drop compact in wet conditions.
Kick to the safe side of teammates.
Value territory when clean possession is difficult.
Adjust the expected landing point.
Communicate wind direction and ball behaviour.

commonErrors.error: Players use normal trajectory into strong wind
commonErrors.correction: Lower the flight and drive through the football.

commonErrors.error: Ball drop becomes loose in wet conditions
commonErrors.correction: Keep the ball closer to the body.

commonErrors.error: Kicker aims directly at the target in a crosswind
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the starting line for expected movement.

commonErrors.error: Team overuses short possession in severe conditions
commonErrors.correction: Take territory when retention becomes low percentage.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to protect the wet football
commonErrors.correction: Use two hands until the kicking action begins.

progressions: Use live weather conditions where safe.
Restrict kicking options according to conditions.
regressions: Explain the required adjustment before each kick.
successIndicators: Maintain effective ball movement in difficult weather.
matchApplication: Replicates the technical and tactical adjustments required during wet, windy or otherwise difficult AFL matches.

title: Wet-Weather Ball Movement
primarySkill: Executing Effective Kicks with a Wet Football
objective: Develop the technical execution and tactical decision making required to move the football effectively in wet and slippery conditions.
setup:
• Dampen the footballs safely.
• Mark boundary-side and central target zones.
• Position players in small teams.
• Begin repetitions from:
• Ground balls.
• Contested marks.
• Loose-ball recoveries.
• Defensive exits.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The coach introduces a wet football into a contested or loose-ball situation.
2. The team winning possession must decide whether to:
3. Complete a short kick.
4. Take territory.
5. Kick to a boundary-side contest.
6. Force a stoppage.
7. Play continues for three to six disposals.
8. Teams score for controlled exits, territory gains and safe stoppages.
9. Dangerous central turnovers are heavily penalised.
10. Reset and rotate starting positions.
coachingPoints: Keep two hands on the football.
Use a compact ball drop.
Shorten the final stride where necessary.
Avoid over-kicking.
Direct long kicks towards safe territory.
Prepare for the ball to spill from marking contests.
Maintain strong ground-level numbers.
Accept stoppages when clean possession is unavailable.

commonErrors.error: Player carries the football in one hand
commonErrors.correction: Secure it with two hands until disposal.

commonErrors.error: Ball is dropped from too high
commonErrors.correction: Shorten and compact the ball drop.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt delicate kicks under heavy pressure
commonErrors.correction: Use a stronger territory kick.

commonErrors.error: Teammates expect clean marks
commonErrors.correction: Prepare front and square for spills.

commonErrors.error: Central options are forced
commonErrors.correction: Use boundary-side territory when conditions reduce control.

matchApplication: Replicates wet-weather football where clean disposal, territory and contest structure become critical.

title: Wind Management Kicking
objective: Develop players’ ability to adjust kicking technique and tactical choices when kicking with, against or across strong wind.
setup:
• Create four stations:
• Kicking with the wind.
• Kicking into the wind.
• Kicking across a left-to-right wind.
• Kicking across a right-to-left wind.
• Include short, medium, long and goal-kicking targets.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Players identify the wind direction before every kick.
2. The kicker announces the intended:
3. Starting line.
4. Trajectory.
5. Landing point.
6. Players execute the kick and assess the result.
7. Receivers adjust their positioning according to the flight.
8. Players rotate through all stations.
9. Finish with a live kicking-possession game using the wind.
coachingPoints: Drive the football lower into the wind.
Avoid allowing the ball to stall.
Control power when kicking with the wind.
Aim into crosswinds rather than directly at the final target.
Position receivers on the expected landing side.
Use the wind tactically for territory.
Adjust set-shot aiming points.

commonErrors.error: Kick is launched too high into the wind
commonErrors.correction: Use a flatter, more penetrating trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Player over-kicks with the wind
commonErrors.correction: Reduce force and control the flight.

commonErrors.error: Kicker aims directly at the target in a crosswind
commonErrors.correction: Start the ball into the wind.

commonErrors.error: Receiver waits at the original target point
commonErrors.correction: Move towards the expected landing area.

commonErrors.error: Players ignore wind when shooting at goal
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the aiming line and kick shape.

progressions: Require both preferred and non-preferred foot kicking.
regressions: Allow practice kicks before scoring begins.
successIndicators: Use the wind to tactical advantage.
matchApplication: Replicates the technical and strategic demands of AFL matches played in strong or changing wind.

title: Fatigue Decision-Making Game
primarySkill: Maintaining Kicking Decisions and Execution Under Fatigue
objective: Develop players’ ability to preserve kicking accuracy, tactical awareness and decision quality during repeated high-intensity efforts.
setup:
• Divide players into two teams.
• Mark three kicking zones and several sprint stations.
• Before entering each possession phase, selected players complete a high-intensity running effort.
• Create short, central, wide and long kicking options.
• Position defenders to apply immediate pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Players complete a prescribed sprint effort.
2. The coach immediately introduces the football.
3. The team in possession must complete a kicking chain.
4. The ball carrier chooses between multiple options.
5. A turnover reverses direction.
6. After each phase, different players complete the fatigue effort.
7. The drill continues in repeated high-intensity blocks.
8. Coaches compare early and late decision quality.
coachingPoints: Recover breathing before disposal where time permits.
Scan during the running effort.
Maintain a compact ball drop.
Avoid automatically kicking long when fatigued.
Communicate more clearly as fatigue increases.
Use teammates to reduce unnecessary physical load.
Preserve team shape late in the drill.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Technical consistency late in the drill.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks immediately without assessing options
commonErrors.correction: Take a settling step and scan where possible.

commonErrors.error: Ball drop becomes uncontrolled
commonErrors.correction: Keep the football close to the body.

commonErrors.error: Players stop communicating
commonErrors.correction: Increase verbal leadership under fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Team structure collapses towards the ball
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width despite physical stress.

commonErrors.error: Players select unnecessarily difficult kicks
commonErrors.correction: Use the highest-percentage available option.

progressions: Require full-ground transition after each possession.
matchApplication: Replicates late-quarter and late-match kicking decisions when physical fatigue affects technical execution and tactical awareness.

title: Communication-Led Kicking
primarySkill: Using Communication to Improve Kicking Decisions
objective: Develop clear, early and specific communication that helps the ball carrier identify pressure, space and the highest-value kicking option.
setup:
• Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
• Mark wide, central and deep target gates.
• Nominate on-field communication leaders.
• Begin play with the ball carrier facing away from the main playing area.

howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier receives possession under pressure.
2. Teammates communicate:
3. Pressure location.
4. Available space.
5. Preferred kick.
6. Time available.
7. The ball carrier turns, scans and selects an option.
8. The possession chain continues for four to six disposals.
9. Points are awarded for:
10. Early communication.
coachingPoints: Communicate before possession arrives.
Use specific information rather than general noise.
Identify pressure direction.
Call the safe side of the receiver.
Confirm whether the player has time.
Use pointing and body language.
Continue communicating after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Leadership when the drill becomes chaotic.

commonErrors.error: Calls arrive after possession
commonErrors.correction: Communicate before the football reaches the player.

commonErrors.error: Players only shout names
commonErrors.correction: Provide information about pressure, space or direction.

commonErrors.error: Multiple conflicting calls confuse the kicker
commonErrors.correction: Establish clear communication priorities.

commonErrors.error: Receivers call for the football while covered
commonErrors.correction: Communicate only when the option is genuinely available.

commonErrors.error: Communication stops after disposal
commonErrors.correction: Continue directing the next phase of play.

howTheDrillWorks:
1. Coach announces the score, time and player-number situation.
2. Teams organise their structure.
3. Play begins from a nominated field position.
4. The team in possession adapts its kicking strategy.
5. The opposition attempts to exploit the numerical situation.
6. The scenario continues until:
7. Time expires.
8. A score occurs.
9. The tactical objective is achieved.
10. Coaches briefly assess decisions before changing the scenario.
coachingPoints: Understand whether possession, territory or speed is required.
Use extra players to create uncontested kicking options.
Avoid exposing central space when outnumbered.
Change tempo according to the scoreboard.
Communicate the spare player’s location.
Recognise when a stoppage is valuable.
Maintain composure during unexpected numerical changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Kicking risk relative to the scenario.

commonErrors.error: Team ignores the numerical advantage
commonErrors.correction: Identify and use the spare player.

commonErrors.error: Players attack recklessly while outnumbered
commonErrors.correction: Protect central space and manage field position.

commonErrors.error: Team retains possession while needing a quick score
commonErrors.correction: Increase tempo and use aggressive options.

commonErrors.error: Players rush while protecting a lead
commonErrors.correction: Use controlled possession and safe kicks.

commonErrors.error: No player communicates the scoreboard
commonErrors.correction: Assign leadership responsibility for time and score.

howTheDrillWorks:

5. Full opposition press.
6. Strong wind.
7. Wet football.

9. Numerical disadvantage.
10. Spare defender.
coachingPoints: Apply all kicking principles without relying on coach direction.
Scan before possession.
Maintain team width and depth.
Recognise numerical and positional advantages.
Change tempo appropriately.
Protect the football in dangerous field positions.
Attack aggressively when advantages appear.
Maintain defensive balance.

commonErrors.error: Team abandons structure under pressure
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce width, depth and positional connection.

commonErrors.error: Players rely on repeated long kicks
commonErrors.correction: Use possession and movement to create better options.

commonErrors.error: Corridor is forced unnecessarily
commonErrors.correction: Balance attacking value against turnover risk.

commonErrors.error: Team slows after creating an advantage

commonErrors.error: Players fail to adapt to new scenarios

Select the correct kick for the situation.
Balance risk and reward.

Communicate with teammates.

Transfer isolated skills into match play.

title: Stationary Handball Fundamentals
objective: Develop a repeatable stationary handball action in which players correctly support the football, strike its lower rear section with a closed fist and direct it towards a controlled target.
groundSize: A flat 10-metre × 10-metre technical area, or one clearly marked station for every two to four players.
equipment: Flat markers or small target cones
Optional handball technique boards or rebound nets
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Simple organisation with minimal observation or intervention
setup:
Mark a safe technical area with adequate spacing between players.
Each player stands with a football and at least two metres of clear space around them.
Players face a cone, line marking, partner or stationary target positioned three to five metres away.
Begin without speed, competition or defensive pressure.
Right-handed players initially place their left foot slightly forward when handballing with the right fist; reverse the stance for the opposite hand.
The coach positions themselves where the support hand, striking fist and ball contact point can be clearly observed.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players begin in an athletic stance with knees slightly flexed, head up and the football supported in front of the body.
On the coach’s instruction, each player forms a compact striking fist with the thumb positioned outside the fingers.
Players place the football on the open supporting hand with the long axis directed towards the target.
The striking fist moves forward from behind the football and contacts its lower rear section.
The supporting hand remains open and stable while the striking arm follows through towards the target.
Players retrieve the football, reset their body position and repeat the action at a controlled tempo.
Complete sets of six to ten repetitions before changing the striking hand.
The coach pauses the group when necessary to demonstrate or correct a common technical fault.
coachingPoints: Hold the football on the open supporting hand rather than gripping it tightly between both hands.
Keep the football in front of the body where the player can see the ball and the intended target.
Form a firm, compact fist with the wrist straight and the thumb safely outside the fingers.
Strike through the lower rear section of the football rather than pushing or carrying it forward.
Keep the supporting hand stable and avoid throwing the football upwards before contact.
Transfer body weight slightly towards the target as the fist moves through the ball.
Finish with the striking fist pointing towards the target.
Prioritise clean contact and legal technique before speed or distance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players begin with a balanced stance and the football positioned in front of the body.
Whether the supporting hand stays open and underneath the football.
Whether the fist contacts the football rather than the supporting hand.
Whether the football leaves the hand from a clear striking action rather than a throw.
Whether the follow-through travels towards the intended target.
Whether players can repeat the technique without rushing or losing body control.

commonErrors.error: The football is tossed or thrown from the supporting hand.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the supporting hand still and require the fist to create the football’s movement.

commonErrors.error: The fist contacts the side or middle of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Mark or point to the lower rear contact area and slow the action until contact improves.

commonErrors.error: The striking wrist bends on impact.
commonErrors.correction: Form a firmer fist and keep the wrist aligned with the forearm.

commonErrors.error: The player grips the football tightly with both hands.
commonErrors.correction: Rest the football on the open supporting palm with only light finger control.

commonErrors.error: The player stands upright with locked knees.
commonErrors.correction: Adopt a balanced athletic stance with soft knees and a slight forward weight transfer.

commonErrors.error: The follow-through finishes across the body.
commonErrors.correction: Direct the fist straight through the football and towards the target.

progressions: Handball towards a partner or stationary target from four to six metres.
Complete consecutive repetitions without pausing between each handball.
Alternate the striking hand after every repetition.
Require players to nominate the target before beginning the action.
regressions: Practise the fist movement without a football.
Hold the football closer to the striking fist to reduce the length of the action.
Use a larger soft football or reduced distance for younger players.
Allow the coach or partner to hold the football lightly while the player practises clean contact.
successIndicators: Support the football on an open and stable hand.
Make clear fist-to-football contact without throwing the ball.
Direct the football towards the intended target.
Demonstrate the basic action with both hands at a controlled speed.
matchApplication: A legal and technically sound handball is the foundation of releasing a teammate, maintaining possession and moving the football through congestion. Players who establish correct supporting-hand position, contact and follow-through are better prepared to execute under movement and pressure later in the chapter.

title: Contact Point and Follow-Through
primarySkill: Clean striking contact and directional follow-through
objective: Develop clean contact on the lower rear section of the football and a straight follow-through that produces controlled, accurate ball flight.
groundSize: Pairs positioned four metres apart within a 15-metre × 15-metre technical area.
equipment: Optional removable ball markers or tape
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players in pairs facing each other four metres apart.
Place one cone beside each player to maintain the correct distance.
One player begins with the football while the partner presents both hands as a target.
Players use a controlled stationary stance.
The coach identifies the lower rear striking area of the football before the drill begins.
Pairs complete separate blocks with the right and left fist.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player with the football establishes a stable support-hand platform.
The player forms a closed fist with a straight wrist and positions it behind the football.
The fist travels directly through the lower rear section of the football.
The player completes the action with the fist pointing towards the partner’s chest.
The receiver secures the football, briefly checks the previous handball’s flight and returns it using the same technique.
Partners complete eight handballs each with one fist.
Players then change the supporting and striking hands for a second set.
The pair counts clean handballs that travel directly to the partner without excessive loop, wobble or sideways rotation.
coachingPoints: Keep the striking fist compact, with the thumb outside the fingers.
Align the wrist with the forearm before and during contact.
Contact the lower rear section of the football to produce forward flight.
Drive through the football rather than stopping the fist at impact.
Follow through directly towards the partner’s chest.
Use a small forward weight transfer rather than leaning backwards.
Maintain a stable supporting hand until the football has left the platform.
Judge quality by clean flight and accuracy, not by how hard the football is struck.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the fist is correctly formed before the action begins.
Whether the wrist remains straight at the point of contact.
Whether contact occurs on the football rather than the support hand.
Whether the football travels with controlled forward rotation rather than excessive wobble.
Whether the follow-through finishes towards the partner.
Whether players maintain the same mechanics with both fists.

commonErrors.error: The fist strikes the middle or top of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the contact point and rehearse the fist path slowly.

commonErrors.error: The wrist bends or turns at impact.
commonErrors.correction: Reset the fist and align the wrist directly behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The action stops immediately after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Extend the fist towards the partner and complete the follow-through.

commonErrors.error: The football floats excessively upwards.
commonErrors.correction: Strike through the lower rear rather than underneath the ball.

commonErrors.error: The football travels across the partner’s body.
commonErrors.correction: Align the platform, fist path and follow-through with the centre of the target.

commonErrors.error: The player tries to create power only with the arm.
commonErrors.correction: Add a controlled weight transfer towards the target.

progressions: Increase the partner distance to five or six metres.
Handball through a one-metre-wide cone gate before reaching the receiver.
Complete five consecutive accurate handballs without resetting the count.
regressions: Reduce the distance to two or three metres.
Use a larger chest-level target such as a handball board.
Pause with the fist positioned behind the football before striking.
Practise the follow-through without a football.
successIndicators: Contact the lower rear section of the football.
Produce controlled and direct ball flight.
Perform the action effectively with both fists.
matchApplication: Clean contact and directional follow-through allow players to release teammates accurately at short and medium distances. This is essential when handballing through congestion, feeding a runner or maintaining possession after winning the football at ground level.

title: Receive at Speed and Release Forward
Boundary Throw-In Fold-Out Handball
primarySkill: Using layered support to exit a boundary throw-in
objective: Develop a boundary-stoppage exit in which midfielders fold away from the contest and use handball to move the football from the boundary into open space.
groundSize: A boundary stoppage area approximately 20 metres × 18 metres with an inside exit lane.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a boundary line and stoppage zone.
Position one first-possession player near the boundary side of the contest.
Place one fold-out support player two to three metres inside.
Position one wider release runner further infield.
Add two controlled-pressure opponents.
Place a finishing receiver 15 metres infield.
The coach feeds the football from a boundary throw-in simulation.
Mirror the activity on both boundaries.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach throws or feeds the football into the stoppage.
The first-possession player secures the football near the boundary.
The fold-out support player moves laterally and slightly backwards into clear space.
The first-possession player protects the football and handballs to the fold-out player.
The wider runner accelerates infield.
The fold-out player receives facing the centre of the ground.
The second handball releases the wider runner.
The runner connects with the finishing receiver.
Pressure players attempt to close the inside exit without exceeding contact restrictions.
Rotate roles and repeat from the opposite boundary.
coachingPoints: The boundary-side player must recognise the reduced space.
Fold-out support should move away from the contest, not towards it.
The first handball should be short and protected.
The fold-out player should receive with vision towards the centre.
Wider support must remain separated from the stoppage.
Use the hand that directs the football away from boundary pressure.
The second handball should lead the runner infield.
Players must avoid forcing the exit when the lane is closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the first-possession player protects the football.
Whether fold-out support creates genuine separation.
Whether the first handball remains short and controlled.
Whether the second receiver holds infield width.
Whether body orientation supports the infield release.
Whether the football exits the stoppage in possession.
Whether the pattern works from both boundaries.

commonErrors.error: Fold-out support moves back into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally and backwards into clear infield space.

commonErrors.error: The first-possession player handballs along the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Use the infield support angle when available.

commonErrors.error: The fold-out receiver faces the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the centre before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Wider support starts too close to the stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Hold separation until the first handball is completed.

commonErrors.error: The second handball forces the receiver sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Lead the runner towards the centre.

commonErrors.error: The exit is attempted through a closed lane.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession or use an alternate support option.

progressions: Begin from a live boundary throw-in.
Allow the first-possession player to choose between two fold-out options.
Require a forward kick after the exit.
Progress to match-like contact for suitable groups.
successIndicators: Protect and release the first possession.
Exit the stoppage in controlled possession.
matchApplication: Boundary stoppages compress available space. Folding one player away from the contest creates a short outlet and can shift the football into the centre before opposition pressure resets.

title: Wing Fold and Inside Return
primarySkill: Using a wing fold and inside return handball to change the running lane
objective: Develop a wing possession pattern in which the outside player releases an inside runner and receives the football back beyond pressure.
groundSize: A wing corridor approximately 30 metres long and 15 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Player A begins wide with the football.
Player B begins inside and slightly behind.
Player C starts further forward in the wide lane.
Add one shadow defender between Player A and Player C.
Mark an inside support channel and outside return channel.
Player A must use Player B before regaining possession outside.
Mirror the pattern on both wings.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A carries forward in the wide lane.
Player B accelerates from inside and behind.
Player A handballs to Player B.
Player A immediately folds behind and then outside Player B.
Player B receives and engages the shadow defender.
Player B returns the football into Player A’s outside run.
Player A receives beyond the defender and handballs to Player C.
Players follow their disposal and rotate.
Repeat on both wings.
Increase tempo only when running lines remain separate.
coachingPoints: Inside support should arrive from behind the ball carrier.
The first handball must be short and accurate.
The original ball carrier should fold behind before moving outside.
Player B should engage the defender before returning the football.
The return handball must lead Player A into the outside lane.
Running lines should remain clearly separated.
Use the correct hand for each direction.
Continue forward after breaking the pressure line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether Player B times the inside support run.
Whether Player A folds behind rather than crossing in front.
Whether Player B draws the defender.
Whether the return handball leads the outside runner.
Whether the final connection remains accurate.
Whether both wings are used effectively.

commonErrors.error: Player B begins ahead of the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Start slightly behind and accelerate into the inside lane.

commonErrors.error: Player A crosses in front of Player B.
commonErrors.correction: Fold behind before moving into the outside lane.

commonErrors.error: Player B returns the football immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Carry until the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: The return handball goes behind Player A.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target the outside running path.

commonErrors.error: Players collide or occupy the same line.
commonErrors.correction: Use the marked inside and outside channels.

commonErrors.error: The pattern slows after the return handball.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate beyond the defender and connect forward.

progressions: Allow Player B to choose between returning outside and continuing inside.
successIndicators: Fold behind into the outside lane.
Draw the defender before the return.
matchApplication: Wing players can use an inside teammate to draw pressure and regain possession outside. The fold-and-return pattern creates overlap while maintaining width and forward momentum.

title: No-Look Support Handball Decision
primarySkill: Using pre-possession scanning to release support without prolonged visual confirmation
objective: Develop the ability to scan support before possession arrives and complete a rapid handball based on confirmed movement and communication rather than staring at the final target.
groundSize: Stations approximately 14 metres long and ten metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Organise groups of four: feeder, receiver-ball carrier and two support players.
The receiver-ball carrier begins facing the feeder.
Support players stand behind and to either side of the receiver.
Before the feed, only one support player moves into the active lane.
The receiver must scan over both shoulders before the football arrives.
One shadow defender may stand in front to restrict prolonged turning.
Rotate roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both support players begin in their starting positions.
The receiver scans over each shoulder.
One support player moves into space and calls.
The feeder delivers the football to the receiver.
The receiver secures possession while facing the feeder.
Using the earlier scan and communication, the receiver organises the football and handballs to the active support player.
The player may use a brief peripheral check but should not complete a full turn before release.
The support player catches and exits through a gate.
One point is awarded for the correct option and accurate delivery.
Rotate roles after four repetitions.
coachingPoints: Scan both shoulders before the football arrives.
Confirm the support player’s movement and voice.
Secure the football cleanly before release.
Maintain awareness of pressure in front.
Use peripheral vision rather than blindly disposing.
Select the hand aligned with the known support side.
Keep the release compact and legal.
This is an awareness drill, not permission to handball without reliable information.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the receiver scans before the feed.
Whether the active support player communicates.
Whether the correct target is selected.
Whether the receiver uses enough visual confirmation to avoid blind disposal.

commonErrors.error: The receiver does not scan before possession.
commonErrors.correction: The feeder must wait for two visible shoulder checks.

commonErrors.error: The player handballs blindly based only on a voice.
commonErrors.correction: Require prior visual confirmation and a brief peripheral check.

commonErrors.error: The receiver turns fully and delays release.
commonErrors.correction: Use the pre-possession scan to organise the handball sooner.

commonErrors.error: The incorrect support player is selected.
commonErrors.correction: Identify colour, position and voice before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: The handball is rushed before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Complete clean two-hand control before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players use the drill as a trick rather than an awareness task.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that reliable information must exist before release.

progressions: Add a second moving support option.
Delay the support movement until immediately before the feed.
Require release within one second of possession.
Begin with an imperfect handball feed.
regressions: Allow the receiver to turn partially.
successIndicators: Confirm the option through communication or peripheral vision.
matchApplication: Elite players scan before receiving so they can release rapidly when pressure arrives. The skill depends on accurate prior information and communication, not on disposing without awareness.
relatedDrills: HB-035 – Handball Square with Moving Choice

title: Elite Handball Decision and Execution Assessment
Fatigued Stoppage Repeat Scenario
primarySkill: Executing repeated stoppage handball exits under fatigue
objective: Develop the ability to maintain stoppage role discipline, legal handball technique and decision quality across repeated high-intensity contest efforts.
groundSize: A stoppage area approximately 25 metres × 25 metres with two exit corridors.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two midfield groups.
Mark a central stoppage circle and two exit corridors.
Begin with a live or controlled ball-up.
Each repetition lasts until a clean exit or turnover.
Players immediately complete a short recovery run and return for the next stoppage.
Roles rotate between first possession, close support, outside release and pressure.
Work in blocks of four to six stoppages.
Provide planned recovery between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach initiates the first stoppage.
Players contest for possession.
The winning team attempts to complete a handball exit through either corridor.
The opposition applies match-like pressure.
When the repetition ends, players complete the nominated recovery run.
Teams immediately reorganise for the next stoppage.
Repeat four to six times within the block.
Record successful exits, illegal disposals and role errors.
Provide recovery and one technical correction.
Repeat the block with changed roles or exit conditions.
coachingPoints: Re-establish roles before every stoppage.
Fatigue must not remove first-, second- and third-possession structure.
Protect the football before releasing.
Use short, direct handballs in congestion.
Outside support must continue to hold width.
Maintain legal technique when breathing and heart rate are elevated.
Recovery running should not prevent safe contest preparation.
End the block if technique or contact standards deteriorate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether roles are reorganised between repetitions.
Whether players default to the dominant-hand side.
Whether players apply the correction in the next block.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to reorganise before the next stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Assign roles during the recovery run.

commonErrors.error: Handballs become throws under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the block and restore the legal support platform and strike.
