Require a switch through two different disposal types.
regressions: Begin with a clear weak-side numerical advantage.
Allow the coach to call the switch.
successIndicators: Exploit the spare side with controlled possession.
matchApplication: Teams can create space away from the football by attracting defenders through credible possession. The switch becomes valuable only after the opposition has committed enough numbers to create a genuine spare side.

title: Leadership Call and Player Override
primarySkill: Responding intelligently to tactical leadership calls
objective: Teach players to follow clear leadership calls when they suit the game picture while retaining responsibility to override or modify the call when immediate information makes it unsafe or ineffective.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Nominate a captain and one line leader for each team.
Establish several simple calls, such as:
Switch.
Control.
Fast.
Boundary.
Corridor.
Hold.
Begin each passage from a different field position.
The opposition may change its shape after the leadership call.
Leaders cannot cancel or modify the call after the ball carrier begins the action.
howTheDrillWorks:
A team begins with possession.
The captain or line leader makes a tactical call.
Players begin reorganising according to the call.
The opposition then adjusts its shape or pressure.
Ball carriers and nearby players must determine whether the original call remains appropriate.
When the call remains suitable, the team executes it collectively.
When immediate pressure makes it unsafe, the ball carrier may override or modify the action.
Two points are awarded for correctly executing a suitable leadership call.
Two points are also awarded for a justified override that preserves or improves possession.
An unjustified override or blind obedience that causes a turnover gives the opposition two points.
Review the reasoning between passages.
Rotate leadership roles regularly.
coachingPoints: Leadership calls provide a shared method, not an excuse to ignore live information.
Players should follow the call unless a clear immediate reason prevents it.
Overrides must be based on pressure, lane closure, numbers or field position.
Communicate the override quickly so teammates can adjust.
Avoid changing the method because of personal preference.
Leaders should make early, simple and specific calls.
Players remain accountable for the final action.
Review whether the call or execution caused the outcome.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether leadership calls are early and clear.
Whether the live game picture is visually confirmed.
Whether players ignore calls without a clear reason.
Whether players follow instructions into obvious pressure.
Whether the team adjusts quickly after an override.
Whether leaders accept and review player decisions.

commonErrors.error: Player follows a call into a closed lane.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the current pressure and passing lane before execution.

commonErrors.error: Player ignores the call because another option is preferred.
commonErrors.correction: Override only when the original method is genuinely unsafe or unavailable.

commonErrors.error: Override occurs without teammate communication.
commonErrors.correction: Use a clear call such as “hold”, “change” or “reset”.

commonErrors.error: Leader makes the call after possession is already pressured.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate before the ball carrier must act.

commonErrors.error: Team blames execution failure on the tactical call.
commonErrors.correction: Separate the quality of the call from the quality of the skill execution.

progressions: Conceal the opposition adjustment from team leaders.
Change score and time during passages.
Increase pressure to full match intensity.
Record leadership and override decisions for video review.
regressions: Tell players when an override will be required.
Allow coaches to support the leader.
successIndicators: Confirm the call against live information.
Override only for clear tactical reasons.
Accept responsibility for the final decision.
matchApplication: Players must respond to captains, line leaders and team calls while still reading the immediate game picture. Effective teams combine collective tactical direction with individual responsibility at the moment of action.

title: Defensive Mismatch Protection
objective: Teach defenders to recognise an unfavourable match-up and decide whether to switch, provide help, protect space or increase pressure on the ball carrier.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use six to twelve attackers against six to twelve defenders.
Create an unfavourable defensive match-up inside forward 50.
Position one potential help defender and one last-line defender nearby.
Begin the attacking possession 50–70 metres from goal.
Vary whether pressure can be applied to the ball carrier.
Defenders are not told in advance whether switching, helping or holding shape will be best.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team gains possession outside forward 50.
Defenders scan match-ups and identify the primary danger.
The direct defender communicates whether help or a switch is needed.
If a safe handover is available, defenders may switch opponents.
If switching would release another dangerous target, a help defender protects the likely disposal space.
When help positioning leaves another option exposed, teammates increase pressure on the ball carrier.
Defenders score one point for preventing the mismatch from receiving cleanly.
Winning possession and exiting defensive 50 scores two additional points.
Attackers score three points for a goal created through the mismatch.
Rotate match-ups and help-defender roles.
coachingPoints: Identify the most dangerous mismatch early.
Communicate before the forward movement begins.
Switch only when responsibilities are clearly transferred.
Help from a position that still allows recovery.
Increase pressure on the ball carrier when defensive coverage is vulnerable.
Avoid sending multiple defenders to the same opponent.
Maintain last-line protection.
Rebound with control after winning possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether help defenders protect the likely space.
Whether another dangerous attacker is released.
Whether pressure on the ball carrier improves.

commonErrors.error: Defenders recognise the mismatch but do not communicate.
commonErrors.correction: Use an early, specific call identifying the opponent and required help.

commonErrors.error: Help defender commits fully and leaves another attacker free.
commonErrors.correction: Position to influence the mismatch while retaining recovery ability.

commonErrors.error: Two defenders switch without confirming responsibilities.
commonErrors.correction: Complete a clear verbal and visual handover.

commonErrors.error: Defenders focus only on the target and allow an unpressured entry.
commonErrors.correction: Increase pressure on the ball carrier to reduce disposal quality.

commonErrors.error: All defenders collapse and leave no rebound outlet.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one defender or outside player in a release position.

progressions: Allow attackers to rotate and create new mismatches.
Begin from turnovers and repeat entries.
Require player leaders to organise all defensive adjustments.
regressions: Predetermine whether to switch or help.
Reduce the number of attacking targets.
successIndicators: Maintain coverage of other dangerous options.
Apply pressure to the ball carrier.
matchApplication: Defensive match-ups change through rotations, injuries, transition and opposition tactics. Teams must recognise when help or switching is required without creating a larger problem elsewhere.

title: Weather-Adjusted Decision Game
primarySkill: Adjusting decisions to weather and ground conditions
objective: Develop players’ ability to adjust disposal type, possession method, field positioning and risk according to wind, rain, slippery ground or reduced visibility.
equipment: Water spray for footballs where safe
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Use two balanced teams.
Prepare safe scenario conditions representing:
Strong wind towards one end.
Crosswind.
Wet or slippery football.
Slower ground movement.
Reduced marking reliability.
Do not create unsafe footing or uncontrolled wet surfaces.
Mark territory gates, short-possession zones and ground-level support areas.
Begin from varied field positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces or introduces the current weather condition.
Teams play towards the scoring end under normal football rules.
Players adjust disposal type, target location and possession method.
Into strong wind, teams may use lower disposals, shorter connections and running support.
With the wind, players judge carry distance and avoid overkicking targets.
In slippery conditions, players anticipate spills and increase ground-level support.
A decision suited to the condition scores one point.
Successful execution scores a separate point.
Unsafe or unrealistic disposal choices give the opposition one point.
Change the condition every three to four minutes.
coachingPoints: Adjust the decision before blaming execution.
Keep kicks lower and more direct into strong wind.
Allow for extra carry with the wind.
Use wider safety margins in a crosswind.
Expect marks and pickups to spill in wet conditions.
Maintain additional ground-level support.
Use territory when clean possession is difficult.
Avoid high-risk central disposals when conditions reduce control.
Protect player safety on slippery ground.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether disposal choices change with conditions.
Whether players adjust kick height and direction.
Whether players continue attempting dry-weather skills in slippery conditions.
Whether central turnover risk is understood.
Whether players communicate wind and ground information.

commonErrors.error: Players use the same disposal method in every condition.
commonErrors.correction: Identify how wind or moisture changes flight, bounce and control.

commonErrors.error: High kicks are used into strong wind.
commonErrors.correction: Use lower, more penetrating disposals and running support.

commonErrors.error: Players stand for marks in wet conditions without ground support.
commonErrors.correction: Position teammates front and centre and defensive side.

commonErrors.error: With-wind kicks travel beyond the target.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce force and allow for additional carry.

commonErrors.error: Players take unnecessary central risk on a slippery football.
commonErrors.correction: Use safer territory and visible support options.

progressions: Use opposing conditions in each half.
Allow player leaders to establish the method.
Continue into a full practice match.
regressions: Work with one condition at a time.
successIndicators: Adjust disposal height, distance and direction.
matchApplication: Weather and ground conditions change the probability and consequence of decisions. Successful teams adapt their method rather than attempting to play identical football regardless of wind, rain or surface quality.

title: Fatigue Decision Integrity
objective: Develop players’ ability to preserve scanning, option selection and team structure as physical fatigue increases.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two teams of six to twelve players.
Position a scoring gate at each end.
Play repeated high-intensity blocks of 60–90 seconds.
Provide short recovery periods.
Require at least one forward, one lateral and one rear support option.
Record decision quality during the first and final 20 seconds of each block.
Adjust work-to-rest ratios for age, fitness and playing level.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams play continuously towards opposite scoring gates.
The coach begins with a contested or transition restart.
Players attempt to maintain scanning and support structure throughout the block.
A correct decision scores one assessment point.
Successful execution scores a separate point.
A rushed disposal, missed scan or structural collapse is recorded.
At the whistle, players recover briefly and receive one coaching question.
Repeat for four to six blocks.
Compare early-block and late-block decision quality.
Reduce workload immediately if technique or player safety deteriorates excessively.
coachingPoints: Continue scanning when breathing and movement become difficult.
Use simple, high-percentage options when skill control reduces.
Avoid confusing fatigue with urgency.
Maintain support behind the football.
Communicate clearly and early.
Reset mentally after errors.
Use body balance before disposal.
Recognise when the team needs controlled possession to recover structure.
Protect decision quality rather than chasing maximum physical output.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether scanning decreases late in blocks.
Whether support becomes flat or disappears.
Whether errors cause further poor decisions.
Whether decision quality improves across repeated blocks.

commonErrors.error: Players stop scanning when fatigued.
commonErrors.correction: Use a visible head-check requirement before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Disposal becomes rushed and unbalanced.
commonErrors.correction: Secure body position before selecting the action.

commonErrors.error: Team loses rear support.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate and communicate one connected player behind possession.

commonErrors.error: Fatigued players attempt increasingly difficult options.
commonErrors.correction: Use simpler possession until control and structure improve.

commonErrors.error: Players mentally disengage after an error.
commonErrors.correction: Focus immediately on the next role and decision.

progressions: Begin each block from a different match phase.
Increase pressure to full match intensity.
Track individual decision accuracy under fatigue.
regressions: Limit the number of consecutive repetitions for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Select options suited to declining control.
Limit the decline in decision quality.
matchApplication: Many decisive moments occur late in quarters and matches when players are fatigued. Teams that preserve scanning, structure and risk control are less likely to concede damaging turnovers.

title: Unscripted Chaos Match
primarySkill: Adapting to unpredictable match events without coach direction
objective: Develop players’ ability to independently solve unpredictable game problems while maintaining team structure, communication and decision quality.
groundSize: Full ground preferred; three-quarter ground minimum.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Use normal positional structures.
Prepare hidden event cards including:
Sudden numerical advantage or disadvantage.
Change of defensive press.
Strong wind direction.
Scoreboard change.
Umpire-call sequence.
Injured-player simulation requiring positional rotation.
Wet-football period.
Reduced time remaining.
Opposition tactical switch.
Assign captains and line leaders.
Coaches introduce events without prescribing the response.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams begin a normal practice match.
Every two to four minutes, the coach introduces an unscripted event.
Players must identify what changed and determine the response.
Captains and line leaders communicate any tactical adjustment.
Coaches do not provide the solution during live play.
One assessment point is awarded when a team recognises the event and responds effectively.
A second point is awarded when the response is coordinated across all lines.
Normal match scoring continues.
Repeated failure to adapt allows the opposition to retain the tactical advantage.
Play continues through turnovers, scores and restarts.
Complete six to eight event changes.
Finish with a player-led review before coach feedback.
coachingPoints: Identify the changed variable before altering team behaviour.
Maintain core principles while adapting the specific method.
Communicate information quickly across the ground.
Avoid waiting for coach direction.
Use leaders without removing individual responsibility.
Reassess whether the response is working.
Separate tactical failure from skill execution error.
Maintain width, depth and turnover protection.
Recover emotionally after unexpected events.
Continue making decisions while fatigued.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Coordination between defenders, midfielders and forwards.
Whether players wait for coach instructions.
Whether the response improves the game picture.

commonErrors.error: Players continue as though nothing changed.
commonErrors.correction: Require leaders to identify and communicate the new variable.

commonErrors.error: Team changes several unrelated elements.
commonErrors.correction: Modify only the behaviours affected by the new problem.

commonErrors.error: One line adapts while others remain unchanged.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the adjustment through each line leader.

commonErrors.error: Players repeatedly look to coaches for answers.
commonErrors.correction: Continue play and review the player-led response afterwards.

commonErrors.error: Tactical method is abandoned after one execution error.
commonErrors.correction: Judge whether the decision remained appropriate before changing again.

progressions: Conceal some information from selected players.
Allow teams to create tactical problems for each other.
Record the match for detailed decision review.
regressions: Introduce one event at a time.
Limit the number of possible tactical changes.
successIndicators: Maintain decision quality under fatigue and pressure.
matchApplication: Matches contain injuries, umpiring decisions, tactical changes, weather shifts, momentum swings and unexpected numerical situations. Players must solve these problems independently while play continues.

title: Decision Making Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Complete application of Australian football decision making
objective: Assess players’ ability to gather information, select effective actions, coordinate team behaviour and adapt to changing match situations across the complete Decision Making chapter.
groundSize: Full ground preferred; three-quarter ground acceptable.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Use full-ground positions and normal match structure.
Prepare assessment phases covering:
Pre-possession scanning.
Space and pressure recognition.
Numerical advantage.
Defensive exits.
Midfield tempo.
Forward entries.
Contested and broken play.
Turnovers and transition.
Team tactical adjustment.
Scoreboard and clock scenarios.
Leadership and player-led adaptation.
Assign coaches or trained observers to different ground areas.
Record decision quality separately from execution.
Use controlled contact suitable to the playing group.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin with a normal match restart.
Allow an initial five-minute period of uninterrupted play to establish natural decision behaviour.
Introduce a defensive-press scenario through a kick-in or defensive possession.
Begin the next passage from a stoppage or contested football.
Introduce a numerical advantage or disadvantage during transition.
Change the defensive structure between man-on-man, zone and hybrid methods.
Include a forward-entry and repeat-entry phase.
Introduce a broken-play situation through a deflection, smother or imperfect football.
Change the score and remaining time for a final-match scenario.
Introduce one unexpected event requiring player-led adaptation.
Award one assessment point for each correct decision.
Award a separate point for successful execution.
Record team-structure decisions including width, depth, support and turnover protection.
Play in five-minute blocks with brief player-led reviews.
Rotate players through defensive, midfield and forward roles.
Complete at least six assessment blocks.
Finish with individual and team feedback based on recurring patterns rather than isolated outcomes.
coachingPoints: Scan before possession and continue scanning while moving.
Recognise teammates, opponents, space, pressure and field position.
Select options that support the next phase, not only the immediate disposal.
Adjust risk to consequence, score and time.
Coordinate leading, holding, clearing and support movement.
Protect possession through pressure and contact.
Connect contested wins to effective first release and transition.
Use corridor, boundary, switch and reset options according to the defensive shape.
Match forward entries to aerial, ground-level and positional advantage.
Recognise defensive bait, traps and hidden pressure.
Manipulate opponents only when it creates genuine advantage.
Respond to leadership calls while retaining personal decision responsibility.
Adapt to weather, fatigue, umpire calls and unexpected events.
Maintain width, depth and protection behind the football.
Judge the decision separately from execution.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Recognition of pressure distance and angle.
Selection between forward, lateral and rear options.
Decisions in congestion and broken play.
Timing of release, carry and evasion.
Recognition of defensive methods and traps.
Whether execution failure is incorrectly treated as decision failure.

commonErrors.error: Players focus only on executing the skill.
commonErrors.correction: Score scanning, recognition and option selection separately.

commonErrors.error: Decision quality collapses as pressure increases.
commonErrors.correction: Rebuild early information gathering and simplify the immediate option.

commonErrors.error: Players use fixed patterns regardless of the opposition.
commonErrors.correction: Change the defensive picture and require live reassessment.

commonErrors.error: Teams lose width, depth or rear support.
commonErrors.correction: Restore complementary movement roles around possession.

commonErrors.error: High-risk actions are selected without considering consequence.
commonErrors.correction: Identify field position, score, time and likely turnover outcome.

commonErrors.error: Players wait for coach instructions during tactical problems.
commonErrors.correction: Use captains and line leaders while preserving individual responsibility.

commonErrors.error: Execution failure causes correct decisions to be abandoned.
commonErrors.correction: Separate the tactical choice from the skill outcome.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after turnovers, umpire calls or errors.
commonErrors.correction: Reassign the next role immediately and continue the phase.

progressions: Remove all coach-created structures and allow teams to create tactical problems.
Conceal score or time information from selected players.
Introduce simultaneous changes in score, numbers and defensive method.
Add repeated high-intensity blocks to test fatigue.
Use video and coded decision analysis.
Complete the assessment within a full practice match.
regressions: Assess one decision category at a time.
Announce the tactical problem before play.
Assign one decision focus to each player.
Use guided questioning before progressing to uninterrupted play.
successIndicators: Select options that improve the next phase.
Adjust risk to field position and match context.
Make productive contested and broken-play decisions.
Maintain team ball movement and defensive balance.
Recognise opposition structures and tactical traps.
Respond appropriately to leadership and umpire calls.
Adapt to fatigue, weather and unexpected events.
Explain the reasoning behind their decisions.
Maintain decision quality across complete match-like phases.
matchApplication: This final assessment integrates the full decision-making demands of Australian football. title: Progressive Jog and Movement Series
objective: Progressively raise body temperature and prepare players for football movement patterns through progressive jog and movement series.
time: Minimum: 6 minutes | Recommended: 8 minutes | Maximum: 10 minutes
setup:
Mark a compact movement area with 4-8 cones and create clear travel lanes.
Split players into groups that allow continuous movement without queuing.
Begin at low intensity and leave enough space for safe changes of direction.
howTheDrillWorks:
Start with easy movement and gradually introduce shuffles, skips, backpedals and controlled direction changes.
Increase range of motion before increasing speed.
Finish with 2-4 sharper efforts that prepare players for the next training activity.
Use the key movement or football pattern of progressive jog and movement series as the main progression rather than adding unrelated exercises.
coachingPoints: Build intensity progressively rather than starting fast.
Keep players tall and balanced through changes of direction.
Use active arms and efficient foot placement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Players should become progressively warmer without visible fatigue.
Movement should become sharper as the drill progresses.

title: Hip Mobility Flow
objective: Improve mobility, joint range and muscular activation before higher-speed football activity using hip mobility flow.
time: Minimum: 6 minutes | Recommended: 8 minutes | Maximum: 10 minutes
setup:
Create small stations or a loose semicircle so every player can see the coach.
Allow approximately one arm span between players.
Use cones only to organise space; the emphasis is controlled quality movement.
howTheDrillWorks:
Move through the mobility pattern slowly enough to maintain posture and control.
Progress from general range-of-motion work into more dynamic football-specific positions.
Finish with active movement rather than prolonged static stretching.
Use the key movement or football pattern of hip mobility flow as the main progression rather than adding unrelated exercises.
coachingPoints: Control range; do not force mobility.
Maintain neutral posture and stable trunk position.
Move smoothly from mobility into active running.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Range of motion should improve without compensation or discomfort.
Players should remain controlled rather than rushing repetitions.

commonErrors.error: Forcing range of motion.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain posture, follow structural cues, and control movement intensity.

commonErrors.error: Holding static stretches for too long immediately before high-speed work.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain posture, follow structural cues, and control movement intensity.

commonErrors.error: Rushing through movements without control.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain posture, follow structural cues, and control movement intensity.

progressions: Add controlled movement between mobility exercises.
Combine two mobility patterns into one flow.
successIndicators: Players demonstrate increased range and control.
matchApplication: Improves movement readiness for low positions, reaching, turning and repeated football actions.

title: Running Mechanics Preparation
objective: Prepare players for AFL acceleration, deceleration and high-speed movement demands through running mechanics preparation.
time: Minimum: 8 minutes | Recommended: 10 minutes | Maximum: 12 minutes
setup:
Set acceleration and deceleration lanes with clear start and finish markers.
Keep groups small so each player receives frequent repetitions with adequate recovery.
Use a safe run-off area beyond the final marker.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin with technical running actions at approximately 60-70% intensity.
Build each repetition progressively toward 85-95% where appropriate.
Include controlled braking and re-acceleration so players are prepared for AFL movement demands.
Use the key movement or football pattern of running mechanics preparation as the main progression rather than adding unrelated exercises.
coachingPoints: Prioritise posture, shin angle and foot strike.
Accelerate smoothly and decelerate under control.
Avoid maximal speed before players are physically prepared.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Running technique should remain stable as intensity rises.
Players should decelerate without excessive reaching, collapsing or slipping.

commonErrors.error: Going maximal before completing progressive build-ups.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain posture, follow structural cues, and control movement intensity.

commonErrors.error: Overstriding during acceleration.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain posture, follow structural cues, and control movement intensity.

commonErrors.error: Stopping upright instead of lowering into deceleration.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain posture, follow structural cues, and control movement intensity.

successIndicators: Players complete high-quality accelerations and decelerations.
Running mechanics remain stable at higher speed.
Players finish ready for speed or football work.
matchApplication: Prepares acceleration, braking and re-acceleration actions used in contests, leads and defensive pressure.

time: Minimum: 6 minutes | Recommended: 8 minutes | Maximum: 10 minutes
setup:
Organise players in pairs or small groups with enough footballs to minimise waiting.
Use short, accurate disposal distances initially.
Mark movement channels so players receive, dispose and continue moving.
howTheDrillWorks:
Keep the football moving continuously with players following their disposal or rotating to the next position.
Begin with short, clean skills and gradually increase speed, distance or decision pressure.
Demand communication and movement immediately after disposal.

coachingPoints: Clean hands and accurate disposal before increasing pace.

Encourage communication on every repetition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Skill errors should reduce as touch and movement rhythm improve.
Players should stay active between possessions rather than standing.

title: Mirror Movement Competition
objective: Raise intensity and competitive focus safely through mirror movement competition without turning the warm-up into a full-contact contest.
time: Minimum: 5 minutes | Recommended: 7 minutes | Maximum: 9 minutes
setup:
Create short competitive lanes or grids and pair players by similar speed and size.
Clearly define start, finish and safety boundaries.
Keep contact controlled and use quick rotations to avoid excessive early fatigue.
howTheDrillWorks:
Run short competitive repetitions of 3-8 seconds.
Reward reaction, clean movement and control rather than reckless contact.
Rotate opponents frequently and keep recovery short but sufficient for movement quality.
Use the key movement or football pattern of mirror movement competition as the main progression rather than adding unrelated exercises.
coachingPoints: Compete hard but stay technically controlled.
Keep repetitions short enough to maintain quality.
Match players sensibly and avoid unnecessary early contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Competitive intent should rise while technical control remains intact.
Players should finish repetitions alert rather than fatigued.

title: Attacking Shape Foundations
primarySkill: Establishing an effective attacking shape around the football.
objective: Develop players’ understanding of how to form and maintain a balanced attacking shape that provides forward, lateral and release options for the player in possession.
groundSize: A rectangular area approximately 40 metres long by 30 metres wide, divided into three horizontal zones.
equipment: Three marker poles or cone gates
setup:
Divide players into two attacking groups of equal size.
One group operates at a time while the other group observes or completes a separate ball-handling activity.
Place one starting player with the football at one end of the area.
Position three to five teammates ahead of the football across the width and depth of the area.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
No defenders are used initially.
Players must avoid standing in a straight horizontal or vertical line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The starting player begins with the football and scans the attacking shape ahead.
Teammates establish at least one forward option, one lateral option and one release option behind or beside the football.
The football is moved by kick or handball through the area while all players adjust their positions after every disposal.
The player who disposes must immediately move to create another support option rather than remaining stationary.
The group scores by carrying or disposing the football through the scoring gate without two attackers occupying the same running lane.
Players reset at the opposite end and repeat in the other direction.
After several repetitions, introduce a five-second limit for the player in possession.
Rotate the observing group into the activity.
coachingPoints: Create options in front of, beside and behind the player in possession.
Avoid forming a flat line across the ground.
Maintain enough separation for each player to remain a genuine disposal option.
Adjust immediately when the football changes position.
Communicate early using names, direction and available space.
The nearest player should provide quick support without crowding the ball carrier.
Players further from the football should maintain width and depth.
Continue moving after disposing of the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players establish multiple disposal angles before the ball carrier comes under pressure.
Whether players maintain width and depth rather than following the football.
Whether the disposer moves again after releasing the football.
Whether players communicate before the football arrives.
Whether the attacking shape adjusts as possession moves through each zone.
Whether players can identify when the shape has become too flat or congested.

commonErrors.error: All players move towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Hold wider players in their lanes and require one player to remain ahead of the football.

commonErrors.error: Players form a straight line across the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger starting positions so each player is at a different depth.

commonErrors.error: The disposer stops after releasing the football.
commonErrors.correction: Require the disposer to run past, support behind or replace another player’s position.

commonErrors.error: Players call for the football after the ball carrier has already committed.
commonErrors.correction: Demand earlier communication and scanning before possession is received.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand too close together.
commonErrors.correction: Use cones to identify minimum spacing until players recognise the required distance.

progressions: Add one passive defender who applies shadow pressure to the player in possession.
Add a second defender who attempts to close the most obvious passing lane.
Require the group to use both sides of the area before scoring.
Introduce a turnover consequence if two attackers occupy the same lane.
Allow defenders to become fully active once the attacking shape is consistently maintained.
regressions: Use handball only over a smaller area.
Mark fixed starting positions for forward, lateral and release options.
Pause after each disposal and allow the coach to reposition players.
successIndicators: Provide at least three different disposal angles.
Move immediately after disposing of the football.
Reach the scoring gate without the shape collapsing around the ball carrier.
matchApplication: The drill introduces the basic attacking structure required whenever a team wins possession. Effective teams provide the ball carrier with options ahead of the football, across the ground and behind the contest. Maintaining this shape reduces congestion, improves possession retention and allows the team to move the football towards goal without relying on a single predictable option.
relatedDrills: DM-100 – Decision Making Chapter Final Assessment

title: Contact and Release Chain
primarySkill: Maintaining an attacking disposal chain through controlled contact.
objective: Teach players to remain composed through controlled contact and release possession to connected support without losing attacking momentum.
groundSize: A 35-metre-long by 20-metre-wide channel with three contact stations.
setup:
Mark three staggered contact stations through the channel.
Position one defender or pad holder at each station.
Divide attackers into groups of four.
Begin the football with the first attacker.
Position support runners behind and beside possession.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
Rotate contact roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first attacker carries towards the opening contact station.
The defender applies controlled body pressure.
The ball carrier protects possession and releases to a support runner.
The receiver continues towards the next contact station.
The previous disposer follows and becomes the next support option.
The sequence repeats through all three stations.
Support players must remain on different angles.
The group scores by reaching the final gate without a fumble or turnover.
Defenders may increase pressure gradually as technique improves.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Lower the centre of gravity before contact.
Keep the football away from the defender.
Maintain balance through the contact.
Release before the tackle becomes complete.
Support players should remain visible.
The disposer must continue running.
Communicate the next support option early.
Avoid blind or backward handballs.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the ball carrier braces safely.
Whether support players maintain clear angles.
Whether the release occurs before control is lost.
Whether the disposer follows the football.
Whether technique remains composed under repeated contact.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier holds the football too long.
commonErrors.correction: Encourage earlier recognition and release.

commonErrors.error: Support runners move directly behind possession.
commonErrors.correction: Create angled support lanes.

commonErrors.error: The football is exposed to the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Carry on the protected side and use the body as a shield.

commonErrors.error: The disposer stops after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate follow-up running.

commonErrors.error: Players rush the handball before balance is established.
commonErrors.correction: Secure footing and control before release.

progressions: Replace pads with controlled live defenders.
Add a second defender at the final station.
Require players to choose between two support options.
Continue into a live scoring action.
successIndicators: Maintain execution across repeated contact efforts.
matchApplication: Attacking possession frequently continues through tackles, bumps and body pressure. Players must protect the football and release to support before the defence can create a stoppage or turnover.
relatedDrills: TK-120 – Tackling and Pressure Chapter Final Assessment
TO-013 – Numbers at the Contest Exit

title: Smother Recovery Connection
primarySkill: Recovering and reconnecting after an attacking disposal is smothered.
objective: Teach players to react immediately to a smothered kick or handball and create a connected second attacking possession.
groundSize: A 35-metre-long by 25-metre-wide area with a disposal zone and two recovery lanes.
setup:
Position one ball carrier inside the disposal zone.
Position one defender close enough to pressure or smother.
Place two attacking support players in separate recovery lanes.
Position one additional defender beyond the zone.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
The initial defender alternates between allowing the disposal and attempting a controlled smother.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives and prepares to dispose.
The defender applies immediate pressure and may attempt a controlled smother.
Support players remain active on separate angles.
If the disposal clears the defender, play continues towards the scoring gate.
If the football is smothered, the ball carrier and support players react immediately.
The nearest attacker attempts to recover the loose football.
Other attackers provide outside and rear support.
The second defender applies pressure to the recovery possession.
Attackers score two points for recovering the smother and reaching the gate.
Defenders score by winning the loose football and exiting through a side gate.
Reset after each outcome.
coachingPoints: Expect pressure on the disposal.
Support should remain active until the football clears the contest.
The original disposer must react immediately to the smother.
One player attacks the loose football while others spread.
Protect the recovery possession before releasing.
Avoid repeating the same blocked disposal line.
Use the recovery to change the attacking angle.
Apply pressure immediately if defenders win the loose football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether support players stop when the disposal begins.
Whether the original disposer reacts after the smother.
Whether one attacker takes responsibility for recovery.
Whether support forms on different angles.
Whether the next disposal avoids the original pressure line.

commonErrors.error: Players assume the disposal will clear the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain active support until the football is safely released.

commonErrors.error: The original disposer stands still after the smother.
commonErrors.correction: Demand an immediate second effort.

commonErrors.error: Several attackers collide at the loose football.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate the nearest player to recover while others spread.

commonErrors.error: The recovery disposal follows the same blocked path.
commonErrors.correction: Change the angle through lateral or rear support.

commonErrors.error: Attackers stop if defenders recover first.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and prevent the exit.

progressions: Make the smother defender fully active.
Continue into a live scoring phase.
Add repeated smother and spoil scenarios.
regressions: Predetermine whether the disposal will be smothered.
matchApplication: Smothers create unpredictable loose footballs and rapid changes in advantage. Teams that react first and remain connected can recover the possession and continue attacking before defenders reorganise.

title: Centre-Bounce Scoring Chain
primarySkill: Converting centre-bounce possession into a coordinated scoring opportunity.
objective: Develop a complete attacking chain from centre-bounce possession through midfield exit, forward connection and scoring-method selection.
groundSize: Centre square to the attacking goal using full forward-half width.
setup:
Use realistic centre-bounce numbers.
Position rucks and midfielders inside the centre square.
Position wings outside the square.
Position forwards and defenders in normal attacking-half roles.
Use normal goals.
Begin every repetition with a centre bounce or controlled ball-up.
Assign one team as the primary attacking team for three repetitions before rotating.
Allow legal match-like contact appropriate to the playing group.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin with a centre bounce.
Midfielders compete to win or receive the stoppage possession.
As possession is secured, attacking midfielders spread into forward, lateral and release lanes.
Wings adjust according to the exit side.
Forwards coordinate short, deep and clearing leads.
The ball carrier selects a direct entry, high-forward connection, handball surge or reset.
Play continues until a score, turnover or defensive exit.
Normal match scoring applies.
Award one bonus point for a clean centre-bounce exit.
Award another bonus point when the exit creates a controlled scoring opportunity.
If defenders win possession, they counterattack towards the opposite end gate.
Reset immediately for the next centre bounce.
Rotate ruck, midfield and forward roles after each block.
coachingPoints: Establish the intended exit before the bounce without becoming predictable.
Spread immediately after possession is won.
Wings must react to the actual exit rather than pre-empt it.
Forwards should coordinate movement with the midfield possession.
Protect the first possession before forcing an entry.
Use the high-forward connection when the direct route is covered.
Maintain support behind the ball carrier.
React immediately if the opposition wins the stoppage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether midfielders create separate exit lanes.
Whether wings adjust to possession direction.
Whether forwards time their leads correctly.
Whether the ball carrier has multiple entry choices.
Whether the team maintains support behind possession.
Whether the attack creates a quality shot rather than a rushed entry.
Whether transition response is immediate after a lost stoppage.

commonErrors.error: Midfielders remain clustered after the stoppage win.
commonErrors.correction: Assign forward, lateral and release spread responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Wings commit before possession direction is clear.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width and react to the actual exit.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead before midfield control is established.
commonErrors.correction: Trigger movement when the first possession is secured.

commonErrors.error: The first ball carrier kicks blindly inside 50.
commonErrors.correction: Use the high-forward or release option when the direct entry is covered.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after a lost centre bounce.
commonErrors.correction: Make defensive transition part of the scoring system.

progressions: Begin with the attacking team trailing late in the match.
Add a required scoring time limit.
Remove all coach communication during the repetition.
regressions: Pause after the stoppage win to organise spread.
matchApplication: Centre-bounce wins provide valuable scoring opportunities because both teams begin in structured positions. The advantage depends on clean exit, rapid spread and coordinated movement before the opposition can establish defensive support.
relatedDrills: RK-080 – Ruck and Stoppage Craft Chapter Final Assessment

title: Protect Lead and Counterattack
primarySkill: Protecting a late lead while remaining ready to counterattack.
objective: Teach players to retain possession and protect field position while recognising opportunities to counterattack and extend a late-game lead.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Set one team between one and twelve points ahead.
Set the clock between two and four minutes.
Begin the leading team in possession from varied field positions.
Use normal rules, boundaries and scoring.
Nominate time and field-position leaders.
The trailing team applies aggressive pressure.
Repeat with different leads and starting positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The leading team begins in possession.
Players assess whether to retain, advance, score or use the boundary.
The team maintains width and support behind possession.
If the opposition overcommits, attackers may launch a counterattack.
A counterattack should be taken only when the scoring chance is clear and turnover protection remains.
Turnovers are played live.
The scenario ends when time expires or the trailing team takes the lead.
Reset with a different score, time and field position.
Rotate leadership roles.
Coaches record risk decisions without interrupting play.
Review selected decisions.
Repeat the scenario under greater pressure.
coachingPoints: Know the score and remaining time.
Maintain active possession rather than standing still.
Use safe width, rear support and boundary positions.
Avoid unnecessary central turnovers.
Recognise when aggressive opposition pressure creates counterattacking space.
Counterattack with enough support to protect possession.
Take a clear score that extends the lead.
Maintain defensive balance behind every attacking action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether possession remains active and connected.
Whether players choose suitable field positions.
Whether the team becomes excessively defensive.
Whether enough players support the counterattack.
Whether defensive balance remains behind possession.

commonErrors.error: Players refuse every forward option.
commonErrors.correction: Take clear opportunities that extend the lead without excessive risk.

commonErrors.error: The team attacks centrally despite scoreboard control.
commonErrors.correction: Use safer width or boundary possession unless the central option is clearly open.

commonErrors.error: Players become stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Continue providing safe leads and replacement movement.

commonErrors.error: Too many players join the counterattack.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain defenders and rear support behind possession.

commonErrors.error: A counterattack begins without a genuine advantage.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until the defence overcommits.

progressions: Run repeated scenarios with limited recovery.
regressions: Give the leading team a numerical advantage.
Pause after turnovers to assess risk.
successIndicators: Preserve defensive balance until time expires.
matchApplication: Protecting a lead does not require abandoning attack. Effective teams control possession, manage field position and punish opposition overcommitment without exposing themselves to unnecessary turnover risk.
relatedDrills: TO-015 – Fast or Control Tempo Game

title: Rotating Match Scenario Circuit
primarySkill: Applying team offence across varied match scenarios.
objective: Prepare players to adapt their attacking method across a sequence of realistic match scenarios without losing the core principles of width, depth, connection and support.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare scenario cards including:
Centre-bounce attack.
Kick-in to score.
Defensive turnover transition.
Boundary pressure escape.
Forward-half repeat entry.
Two-minute comeback.
Protecting a late lead.
Wet-weather possession.
Reduced-bench fatigue.
Attack against a changing defensive system.
Use normal match rules and scoring.
Assign line leaders and scoreboard communicators.
Rotate the starting scenario every four to six minutes.
Allow appropriate recovery and safety adjustment between high-load blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
Draw or select the first scenario.
Position players according to the match situation.
Begin live play.
The attacking team must identify the problem and select an appropriate method.
The defensive team applies realistic pressure and transitions after turnovers.
Normal scoring applies unless the scenario card provides a specific target.
Coaches assess attacking shape, decision quality, communication and outcome.
End the block when the scenario is completed or the nominated time expires.
Provide only brief feedback.
Select a different scenario.
Rotate leadership and specialist roles.
Complete the final two scenarios without coach feedback.
Finish with one unpredictable scenario selected during live play.
coachingPoints: Preserve width, depth and support in every scenario.
Identify the specific match problem quickly.
Select a method suited to score, time, field position and defence.
Communicate the plan across all three lines.
Adapt when the first option is removed.
Maintain possession quality under urgency.
Protect the team behind the football.
Apply immediate transition pressure after turnovers.
Retain core attacking principles when conditions change.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: How quickly players understand each scenario.
Whether line leaders organise the team.
Whether the selected method suits the match problem.
Whether players adapt after the first option closes.
Whether scoreboard and time awareness influence decisions.
Whether performance standards survive repeated scenario changes.

commonErrors.error: Players use the previous scenario’s method in the new situation.
commonErrors.correction: Reassess score, time, field position and defensive structure before restarting.

commonErrors.error: Communication remains local.
commonErrors.correction: Use line leaders to relay the attacking plan across the ground.

commonErrors.error: Urgency causes loss of shape.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width, depth and rear support while increasing decision speed.

commonErrors.error: Players become overly cautious after a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish possession and attack the available opportunity.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue reduces tactical awareness.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the block and restore communication and positioning standards.

commonErrors.error: Core principles disappear when conditions change.
commonErrors.correction: Rebuild around connection, spacing and support before adding tactical detail.

progressions: Change the defensive system during each block.
Reduce recovery between scenarios where safe.
Complete an extended final scenario under full match conditions.
regressions: Announce scenarios before players take position.
Provide the attacking team with a numerical advantage.
Pause midway through each scenario for correction.
successIndicators: Maintain width, depth and rear support.
Manage score, time and field position.
matchApplication: Teams must apply their attacking system in many different match situations. This circuit tests whether players can retain core offence principles while adapting tactics to score, time, field position, conditions and opposition structure.

title: Team Offence Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Applying the complete team-offence system under match conditions.
objective: Assess whether players can independently establish, maintain and adapt complete team offence from possession win through ball movement, forward entry, scoring and turnover response.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams using normal match positions.
Use full-ground dimensions and normal scoring.
Appoint defensive, midfield and forward leaders for both teams.
Prepare varied restarts and scenarios including:
Centre bounce.
Kick-in.
Defensive-half turnover.
Boundary pressure.
Forward-half repeat entry.
Late-game comeback.
Late-game lead protection.
Changing defensive system.
Wet-weather or difficult-ball simulation.
Reduced-rotation fatigue.
Assign coaches to assess separate components of team offence.
Use legal match-like contact appropriate to the playing group.
Provide no tactical coaching during the opening and final blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin with a standard match restart.
Teams play under normal rules for an opening assessment block.
The team in possession must establish width, depth and support ahead, beside and behind the football.
Players select the appropriate route through the ground.
Forwards coordinate scoring threats and entry movement.
Turnovers are played live with immediate transition.
After the opening block, introduce selected match scenarios.
Each scenario continues until a score, turnover, stoppage outcome or time limit.
Normal match scoring applies.
Coaches also record assessment points for:
Establishing attacking shape.
Providing multiple disposal options.
Escaping pressure cleanly.
Advancing all three playing lines.
Using width, corridor, switch and reset appropriately.
Creating and using numerical advantages.
Selecting an effective forward-entry method.
Maintaining two-way scoring threats.
Adapting to defensive systems.
Managing score and time.
Protecting against turnover.
Communicating across all lines.
Provide concise feedback between middle blocks only.
Rotate line leaders and selected positional roles.
Complete a final eight-to-ten-minute block under normal match rules.
Do not provide coach intervention during the final block.
Complete the assessment record after play ends.
coachingPoints: Establish attacking shape immediately after gaining possession.
Maintain width without losing connection.
Provide options at different depths.
Preserve support behind the football.
Select tempo according to numbers, space and pressure.
Use switches and resets to move defensive structures.
Access the corridor only when reward justifies risk.
Coordinate midfield and forward movement.
Maintain aerial and ground-level support.
Adapt to changing defensive systems.
Manage score, time and field position.
Communicate the attacking method across all three lines.
Protect the team against turnover.
Maintain standards under fatigue and match-like pressure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether attacking shape forms without coach direction.
Whether the ball carrier consistently receives several options.
Whether width, depth and rear support remain connected.
Whether players away from the football maintain useful structure.
Whether pressure possessions are released cleanly.
Whether all three playing lines advance together.
Whether switches and resets create improved attacking pictures.
Whether corridor decisions are appropriately balanced.
Whether numerical advantages are identified and used.
Whether forwards coordinate short, deep, clearing and weak-side movement.
Whether scoring-method selection suits the defensive structure.
Whether players adapt to zone, press and man-on-man systems.
Whether scoreboard and time affect risk selection.
Whether leaders organise the team effectively.
Whether turnover protection and transition response are immediate.
Whether execution and decision quality survive fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd possession after winning the football.
commonErrors.correction: Restore forward, lateral, wide and rear support roles.

commonErrors.error: The team becomes flat across the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish staggered depth between playing lines.

commonErrors.error: Weak-side players follow the football.
commonErrors.correction: Hold useful width and remain a genuine attacking threat.

commonErrors.error: Ball movement does not alter the defence.
commonErrors.correction: Change angle, tempo, depth or side with purpose.

commonErrors.error: Players force corridor possession.
commonErrors.correction: Assess receiver separation, next options and turnover consequence.

commonErrors.error: Switches finish with an isolated receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Move all three lines and provide forward, inside and rear support.

commonErrors.error: Forward entries become predictable.
commonErrors.correction: Use varied leading, running, contest and possession methods.

commonErrors.error: Numerical advantages become congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the free player outside defensive pressure.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to adapt to defensive changes.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the new system and select a collective response.

commonErrors.error: Scoreboard urgency causes reckless disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Increase decision speed without abandoning execution quality.

commonErrors.error: The team becomes passive while protecting a lead.
commonErrors.correction: Retain active possession and attack clear opportunities.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes loss of structure.
commonErrors.correction: Rotate roles and return to core spacing and connection principles.

commonErrors.error: Turnovers expose the team behind the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain defensive balance and immediate transition response.

progressions: Remove all scenario warnings and coach prompts.
Change defensive systems during open play.
Add score, time, field-position and numerical-disadvantage conditions.
Use the assessment results to assign individual and line-specific development priorities.
regressions: Assess one phase of team offence at a time.
Provide the attacking team with a numerical advantage.
Pause between phases for structural feedback.
Shorten work blocks for younger, returning or masters players.
successIndicators: Maintain width, depth and rear support.
Advance defensive, midfield and forward lines together.
Use wing, corridor, switch, reset and overload options appropriately.
Coordinate forward movement and scoring threats.
Maintain decision quality and execution under fatigue.
Apply the complete team-offence system without constant coach direction.
matchApplication: This final assessment combines the complete Team Offence chapter from TO-001 to TO-099. It determines whether players can convert possession into organised, adaptable and efficient attack across technical, tactical, pressure, positional and match-scenario demands.
relatedDrills: TO-040 – Team Offence Running Patterns Assessment
TO-060 – Pressure and Contest Mastery Assessment
TO-080 – Team Ball Movement Final Assessment

title: Defensive Shape Foundations
primarySkill: Establishing a connected defensive shape behind the ball.
objective: Develop players’ ability to form, maintain and adjust a compact defensive shape as the football moves across the ground.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge and one main teaching point
setup:
Mark a rectangular playing area with a target gate at each end.
Divide players into an attacking team and a defending team.
Begin with the attacking team holding possession at one end.
Position the defenders between the football and the opposite target gate.
The attacking team moves the football by kick or handball but initially does not attempt to score.
Defenders are restricted to shadow pressure during the first phase.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team circulates the football across and through the area.
Defenders move as a connected unit, maintaining appropriate width, depth and spacing.
When the football moves laterally, the defensive group slides together rather than chasing individually.
The nearest defender applies controlled pressure while teammates protect central and deeper space.
The coach occasionally calls “freeze” and checks the location, spacing and body position of each defender.
After five successful attacking possessions, the attacking team attempts to move the football through the target gate.
Defenders score one point for forcing the attack backwards, wide or into a turnover.
Teams rotate roles after two minutes.
coachingPoints: Maintain a compact shape between the football and the scoring target.
Move when the football moves rather than reacting after the receiver has taken possession.
The nearest defender presses while the next defenders provide cover.
Protect the corridor and force the attack towards wider, less dangerous areas.
Maintain enough spacing to cover ground without creating large gaps.
Communicate the location of opponents, space and possible switches.
Defenders behind the play must scan both the football and their direct opponent.
Reset the shape immediately after every disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether defenders move together or as disconnected individuals.
Whether the nearest defender applies pressure without opening central space.
Whether players communicate before the football arrives.
Whether the defensive line becomes too flat or too stretched.
How quickly the group resets after the football changes direction.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase the football individually.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that one player pressures while the rest protect space and maintain connection.

commonErrors.error: Large gaps appear between defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the area temporarily and set a maximum spacing of 8–10 metres.

commonErrors.error: Defenders watch only the football.
commonErrors.correction: Require players to regularly point to or name their direct opponent.

commonErrors.error: The corridor is left open.
commonErrors.correction: Position the deepest defender centrally and ask the group to force play wide.

progressions: Allow attackers to score immediately through either target gate.
Add an attacking player who begins behind the defensive line.
Introduce live intercepts and controlled tackling.
Award double points for an attacking score through the corridor.
Begin each repetition from a turnover so defenders must recover into shape.
regressions: Use handball only to slow the movement of the football.
Mark defensive reference zones with cones.
Allow the coach to stop play frequently and physically reposition players.
successIndicators: Maintain connected spacing as the football moves.
Protect the corridor before pressuring wide possession.
Identify the pressure, cover and deeper-defender roles.
Reset their shape within two to three seconds of each disposal.
matchApplication: This drill introduces the basic team-defence shape required when the opposition controls possession. It teaches defenders to protect dangerous central space, support the player applying pressure and prevent one disposal from breaking the entire defensive structure.

title: Team Defence Fundamentals Assessment
primarySkill: Applying foundational team-defence principles in an integrated game environment.
objective: Assess whether players can independently apply the foundational team-defence principles introduced in TD-001 to TD-019 during continuous, realistic play.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground, depending on player numbers.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two-thirds or the full ground with normal goals at one end.
Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Position the defence in realistic forward, midfield and deep defensive lines.
Place two wide and two central defensive exit gates.
Prepare a sequence of starting scenarios:
Slow opposition possession
Fast turnover
Wide switch
Outnumbered attack
Forward entry
Failed defensive exit
Assign assistant coaches or leaders to observe specific defensive principles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins each repetition from one of the prepared scenarios.
The attacking team attempts to score using unrestricted football.
The defending team must establish shape, protect dangerous space and apply coordinated pressure.
After a defensive stop, the team attempts to exit through an appropriate gate.
If the exit fails, the coach immediately begins a repeat entry.
Each repetition continues for 45–90 seconds before resetting.
Coaches assess the defence against the nominated success criteria.
Teams swap roles after six repetitions and complete the same scenarios.
coachingPoints: Establish goal-side and central protection immediately.
Maintain connected lines behind the football.
Identify pressure, cover and balance roles around possession.
Force opposition movement towards less dangerous areas.
Communicate opponents, switches, pressure triggers and space behind the play.
Delay when outnumbered and press when support is available.
Reset immediately after failed exits or repeat entries.
Secure possession and select an appropriate defensive exit.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: How quickly the team establishes defensive shape.
Whether the corridor and top of defensive 50 are protected.
Whether pressure is supported by cover and balance.
Whether communication is early and specific.
Whether the team delays correctly when outnumbered.
Whether players reset after repeat entries.
Whether the first exit decision suits the pressure.
Whether the group adapts without direct coach instruction.

commonErrors.error: Players chase opponents without maintaining team shape.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish central protection and connected lines before applying aggressive pressure.

commonErrors.error: Pressure occurs without support.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm pressure, cover and balance responsibilities before the next repetition.

commonErrors.error: Defenders remain passive when a clear trigger appears.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the trigger and require the nearest players to press together.

commonErrors.error: The team fails to reset after an unsuccessful exit.
commonErrors.correction: Use an immediate recovery call and rebuild through goal-side positions.

commonErrors.error: Exit decisions are rushed or repeatedly central.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession, scan and use width when the corridor is congested.

progressions: Require the defence to transition from the exit into a forward entry.
Allow the attacking team to plan its own method for breaking the defensive structure.
regressions: Assess one defensive principle at a time.
Use half-ground rather than two-thirds or full-ground.
Allow defensive leaders to organise the group before each restart.
successIndicators: Establish a connected shape within three seconds of the starting action.
Protect the corridor and central scoring areas.
Recognise and act on pressing triggers.
Secure the defensive stop and select an appropriate exit.
Apply the principles without constant coach direction.
matchApplication: This assessment combines the foundational team-defence behaviours required in Australian football. It measures whether players can organise collectively, protect dangerous space, respond to changing attacking methods, win possession and transition safely out of defence.
relatedDrills: TD-011 – Pressure, Cover and Balance Rotation

title: Tracking and Releasing a Running Opponent
Sliding Line Against Lateral Ball Movement
Defending the Switch Runner
primarySkill: Tracking an opponent who changes from the ball side to the weak side during a switch.
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to recognise, track and hand over an opponent moving across the ground during a change in the direction of possession.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide the area into left, central and right vertical lanes.
Position attackers across all three lanes.
Match defenders to attackers at the start.
Begin with possession in one outside lane.
Nominate one attacker to run from the ball side across to the weak side as the football is switched.
Place three scoring gates at the far end.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins circulating the football on one side.
A nominated attacker runs behind or through the central lane towards the weak side.
The attack switches the football across the ground.
The original defender tracks the runner until a teammate clearly accepts responsibility.
Weak-side defenders adjust centrally before expanding to the new ball side.
The attackers attempt to use the switch runner to score through a gate.
Defenders score one point for completing the handover and two points for preventing the runner’s possession.
Rotate the switch runner and defensive responsibilities after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Scan for opponents moving away from the original ball side.
Track the runner until responsibility is clearly handed over.
Communicate the runner’s name, lane and direction.
Weak-side defenders must prepare to accept the runner before the switch arrives.
Remain goal-side during the handover.
Avoid both defenders following the runner.
Maintain central protection while adjusting to the new ball side.
Pressure the switch kick to reduce its speed and accuracy.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether defenders scan for the crossing runner.
Whether the original defender maintains responsibility.
Whether the weak-side defender prepares early.
Whether communication is specific and acknowledged.
Whether the switch runner receives uncontested possession.

commonErrors.error: Original defender releases the runner too early.
commonErrors.correction: Track until the next defender verbally accepts responsibility.

commonErrors.error: Weak-side defender reacts only after the switch arrives.
commonErrors.correction: Scan and prepare while the football is still on the opposite side.

commonErrors.error: Two defenders follow the same runner.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the handover and require the first defender to return to central cover.

commonErrors.error: Defenders become too wide during the switch.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the corridor before expanding towards the new ball side.

progressions: Remove the nominated runner and allow attackers to choose.
Allow the attack to fake the switch.
regressions: Predetermine the runner and switch direction.
Pause play at the handover point.
successIndicators: Identify runners moving across the ground.
matchApplication: Attacking teams often send runners across the ground during switches to create an extra option on the weak side. Defenders must track and hand over those movements without abandoning the centre of the ground.
relatedDrills: TD-005 – Ball-Side Pressure and Weak-Side Cover

title: Pressure the Receiver on Arrival
primarySkill: Closing a receiver as possession arrives to prevent forward continuation.
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to arrive with controlled pressure as an opponent receives possession, preventing the receiver from turning, accelerating or disposing effectively.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with a target gate at each end.
Position a feeder with two possible receivers ahead.
Place a defender three to five metres from each receiver.
Receivers may lead forward, laterally or back towards the feeder.
Defenders begin goal-side and must read the feeder’s disposal.
Rotate feeding, attacking and defending roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receivers move to create a passing option.
The feeder selects one receiver and disposes by kick or handball.
The defender closes while the football is travelling.
The defender aims to arrive as possession is taken.
If the receiver plays on, controlled tackling becomes live.
The receiver attempts to move through the target gate or release to the second attacker.
Defenders score one point for forcing a backwards disposal and two points for a turnover.
Reset with receivers changing starting positions.
coachingPoints: Read the feeder’s body position before the disposal.
Begin closing as the football is released.
Arrive close enough to prevent the receiver turning.
Decelerate during the final steps.
Maintain goal-side position.
Close the receiver’s preferred disposal side.
Do not make early contact before possession is established.
Recover immediately if the receiver releases the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether defenders read the disposal early.
Whether closing begins during the football’s travel.
Whether receivers are prevented from turning forward.
Whether pressure influences the next disposal.
Whether defenders continue after the ball is released.

commonErrors.error: Defender waits until possession is completed.
commonErrors.correction: Move as soon as the feeder commits to the disposal.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives too fast and overruns.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and decelerate before contact.

commonErrors.error: Defender allows the receiver to turn inside.
commonErrors.correction: Close from the goal-side and protect the central route.

commonErrors.error: Defender contacts before the mark or possession.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain legal pressure and contest only when permitted.

progressions: Allow the feeder to use longer kicks.
Introduce full tackling after play on.
Continue play through multiple consecutive receivers.
successIndicators: Read the disposal before it arrives.
Force sideways, backwards or ineffective disposals.
matchApplication: Defensive pressure is most effective when it arrives with the football. Closing late allows opponents to turn and accelerate, while arriving under control can stop forward momentum and force a predictable disposal.

title: Advanced Pressure and Contest Assessment
primarySkill: Applying advanced defensive pressure and contest principles during continuous match-like play.
objective: Assess whether players can independently combine the advanced pressure and contest behaviours developed through TD-051 to TD-059 across changing field positions and repeated phases.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two-thirds or the full ground.
Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Prepare the following starting scenarios:
Ball carrier under tackle pressure with a nearby release
Loose ground ball with outside support
Pressured kick into an intercept channel
Aerial contest requiring a directional spoil
Attacking crumb inside 50
Boundary stoppage
Repeat forward entries
Position coaches to assess pressure, cover, balance, communication and legal contact.
Rotate teams after completing all scenarios.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins each repetition from one prepared scenario.
The attacking team attempts to retain possession, exit or score.
The defence must apply the correct pressure and contest response without prior instruction.
All spills, smothers, tackles and spoils remain live.
If the attacking team retains possession, the phase continues into another contest.
After winning possession, defenders attempt a controlled exit.
Each repetition lasts 60–120 seconds.
Complete six to eight repetitions before exchanging roles.
coachingPoints: Decide whether the second defender should assist the tackle or protect the release.
Compress around ground balls without losing outside balance.
Use pressure to shape opposition disposals.
Direct spoils away from goal and towards support.
Pressure attacking crumbers immediately.
Close receivers as possession arrives.
Reorganise between consecutive contests.
Protect the corridor at boundary stoppages.
Reset after repeated forward entries.
Maintain safe, legal and disciplined contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether tackle assistance is used appropriately.
Whether the defence retains balance around ground-ball contests.
Whether pressure influences kicks and handballs.
Whether spoils are directed towards safe space.
Whether crumbers and receivers are pressured immediately.
Whether players recover into the next contest.
Whether repeated entries are defended with structure.
Whether defensive wins lead to composed exits.

commonErrors.error: Multiple defenders commit to one contest.
commonErrors.correction: Retain clear pressure, release-cover and balance responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Pressure is applied without influencing the disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Close from an angle that removes the dangerous option.

commonErrors.error: Players watch spoils or loose footballs develop.
commonErrors.correction: Move into the expected second-ball area before the contest finishes.

commonErrors.error: Repeated defensive efforts become unstructured.
commonErrors.correction: Reset roles and goal-side positioning after every phase.

commonErrors.error: Contact technique deteriorates under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate before contact and maintain legal tackling and bodywork.

progressions: Remove all coach explanation before each scenario.
Require the defensive exit to develop into a complete forward entry.
Allow the attacking team to select and repeat the scenario it believes can expose the defence.
regressions: Assess one scenario at a time.
Use controlled rather than match-like contact.
Allow defensive organisation before each restart.
Shorten the work periods and increase recovery.
successIndicators: Apply the correct pressure response to each scenario.
Protect release options while contesting possession.
Maintain balance around ground balls and tackles.
Influence opposition disposals towards defensive support.
Communicate throughout congested and open phases.
Preserve legal contact technique under fatigue.
Win possession and complete an appropriate exit.
